<summary>This title page introduces a 1730 edition of "Christosophia," a seminal collection of mystical and theosophical writings by the German philosopher Jacob Böhme. The work outlines the spiritual journey toward union with the divine through concepts like repentance, "Gelassenheit," and the understanding of human temperaments.</summary>

# CHRISTOSOPHIA,
->or<-
# The Way to Christ,
composed in Nine Small Books,
now condensed into Eight.

---

### The First Book.
### OF TRUE REPENTANCE <note>original Latin: "DE POENITENTIA VERA"</note>,
->or<-
### Concerning True Repentance.
#### The 1st Book.

How a person must awaken themselves within their own will and mind, and what their contemplation and serious purpose should be when they wish to perform powerful repentance; and with what kind of spirit they should step before God when they wish to ask for and obtain forgiveness of sins from God?

### Preface of the Author to the God-loving Reader.

> St. Paul says: Everything that you do, do it in the name of the Lord, and thank God and the Father in Christ Jesus. <note>A translation of Colossians 3:17.</note>

God-loving reader! If you use this little book correctly and make it a matter of earnest sincerity, you will surely experience its benefit. However, I wish to have warned you: if you are not in earnest, then leave the precious names of God alone (through which the highest Holiness is named, stirred, and powerfully desired), so that they do not ignite the wrath of God in your soul. For

An elaborate engraving framed by a double-line border. At the top, a dove representing the Holy Spirit perches on a wooden cross, to which a large anchor is lashed <note>The anchor and cross together symbolize Hope and Faith.</note>. Rays of light emanate from above the dove. Below the cross, a bank of thick clouds parts to reveal a radiant sun-heart. In the center of this heart is a single open eye <note>The "All-Seeing Eye" of God, a common symbol in Böhme’s mysticism representing divine providence.</note>. Above the eye, the biblical citation "Matthew 11:12" is inscribed <note>"And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force."</note>.

To the left of the central heart, a vertical scroll or banner bears the title "The Way to Christ" in Fraktur script. Surrounding the lower part of the radiant heart are two monstrous creatures: a serpent with a star-patterned body on the left, and a winged, clawed dragon on the right. Both appear to be recoiling from or entangled with the light.

At the bottom of the image, the roots of a plant grow into a terrestrial globe. Just above the globe is the citation "Joel 2:12-13" <note>"Even now, declares the Lord, return to me with all your heart... Rend your heart and not your garments."</note>.

<header>IX. The Way to Christ.</header>

one should not misuse the Holy Name of God. This little book belongs only to those who would gladly repent, and who are at the beginning of their desire: they will experience from both sides <note>Meaning both the internal spiritual experience and the external reading of the text.</note> what kind of words are within it, and from what they were born. Herewith, I commend you to the eternal goodness and mercy of God!

### Summaries.

Man’s mind is turned away from God, seeks earthly things, and loves itself, §. 1. It is God’s enemy, 2. and is bound by three chains, which are: God’s wrath, the Devil’s desire, and flesh and blood. 3. Therefore, he should earnestly contemplate death, 4. and God’s righteous judgment, 5. as well as the loss of the Divine Image; 6. likewise the punishment of the damned, 7. and the vain course of the world: 8. in which contemplation he will feel himself in his heart and mind. 9. Whoever now walks in repentance: for them, help is easily found; 10. but whoever stands in conflict within themselves: for them the following process <term>Proceß: Böhme uses this word to describe the methodical "chemical" or spiritual transformation of the soul.</term> is written. 11. Whoever would gladly repent, but finds no true contrition within themselves, 12. must stand in a strict resolve to leave all temporal things without looking back, 13. and suspect nothing evil from the love of Jesus Christ. 14. He should fully imagine within himself the great love of God, 15. that God, in the love of Christ, can will nothing evil, 16. and think that God is present both within and outside of him; 17. also believe that he stands with his soul before the Holy Deity. 18. A short form of confession before God’s eyes. 19. Where the intent is truly earnest, no formula is necessary. 20. God’s process is of many kinds. 21. It may well happen that one does not receive an answer immediately, 22. in which beginning many are ruined. 23. Therefore, there must be a steadfastness, 24. and true earnestness. 25. The soul must woo the Noble Virgin Sophia <note>Sophia is the Greek word for Wisdom. In Böhme's theology, she is the "mirror" of God and the soul's lost heavenly bride.</note> with great desire of love, 26. have a chaste, modest mind, 27. be sober, earnest, and humble, 28. and make a vow to the Noble Sophia. 29. Prayer. 30. Warning to the reader. 31. It must be earnest. 32. The soul must be tested just like Christ, 33. 34. and keep its promise. 35. Humility must be at the forefront against the Devil’s opposition. 36. 37. He who conquers will be crowned. 38. Then comes the contempt of the godless, and even of the very best friends. 39. A very earnest prayer in the trial <term>Anfechtung: A spiritual assault or crisis where the soul feels abandoned by God or attacked by doubt.</term> against God’s wrath in the conscience, and also against flesh and blood, when the Tempter steps to the soul and wrestles with it. 40. Every person must go through judgment. 41. A short formula of prayer when the Noble Sophia kisses the soul with Her love and offers her love. 42. A little prayer for Divine operation, protection, and governance, how the mind should work with and in God in Christ, the Tree of Life. 43. A prayer in and against the trial under the Cross of Christ, at a time when all enemies storm against us, and we are persecuted in the Spirit of Christ, hated, and reviled and blasphemed as evildoers. 44. A little prayer or dialogue between the poor wounded soul

<meta>This page completes the introductory summary of the book's sections and begins the first chapter, "Of True Repentance." It establishes the necessary internal reflection a person must undergo to begin their spiritual journey back to God.</meta>

# 1. Of True Repentance. 3

[...sou]ls and the Noble Virgin Sophia <note>In Böhme’s mysticism, Sophia represents Divine Wisdom, the feminine aspect of God that the soul seeks to reunite with.</note>, in the inward ground of man. 45–51. Warning to the reader. 52. A little morning prayer for when one rises, to commend oneself to God before letting anything else enter. 53. A little evening prayer. 54.

->I.<-

When a person wishes to proceed toward repentance <note>German: *Buße*—this carries the weight of both penance and a deep, transformative change of heart.</note> and turn to God with their prayer, they should, before all prayer, consider their mind <note>German: *Gemüth*—the seat of the soul's disposition and desires.</note>: how it stands entirely turned away from God, how it has become unfaithful to God, and how it is directed only toward the temporal, fragile, earthly life, carrying no true love for God or their neighbor. They should see how it lusts and seethes entirely against God’s commandment, seeking only itself in temporal, fleeting lust of the flesh.

2. Secondly, they should consider how all of this is an enmity against God, which Satan, through his deception, awakened in our first parents <note>Adam and Eve.</note>; for the sake of which abomination we must die the death and let our bodies decay.

3. Thirdly, they should consider the three cruel chains to which our soul is firmly bound during the time of this earthly life. The first is God’s strict wrath, the abyss and dark world, which is the center <term>Centrum: Böhme uses this term to describe the inner core or source from which a person's spiritual nature and "life-fire" originates.</term> and creaturely life of the soul. The second chain is the Devil’s desire toward the soul, with which he constantly sifts and tempts it, seeking without ceasing to plunge it from God’s truth into vanity—such as pride, greed, envy, and wrath—and by his desire, he constantly inflames and ignites these same evil qualities in the soul, whereby the soul’s will turns away from God and enters into a selfhood <note>German: *Selbheit*—the state of being ego-driven or centered on oneself rather than God.</note>. The third and most harmful chain, by which the poor soul stands bound, is the corrupted and entirely vain, earthly, mortal flesh and blood, full of evil desires and inclinations. Here, one should consider how they lie, body and soul, firmly captured in the mire of sin, in God’s wrath in the jaws of hell’s abyss; how God’s wrath burns within them in soul and body, and how they are the stinking swineherd <note>A reference to the Parable of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15, who wasted his inheritance and ended up tending pigs.</note> who has squandered and consumed his father’s inheritance—namely, God’s love and mercy—with the Devil’s fatted swine in earthly pleasure; and has not noticed...

<meta>This page continues the list of points for self-reflection before prayer, specifically addressing the soul's loss of its original divine state and the terrifying reality of judgment. It completes point 3 and covers points 4 through 6.</meta>

<header>IX. The Way to Christ.</header>

[...and how the soul] has forgotten the precious covenant and reconciliation of the innocent suffering and death of **Jesus Christ**, which **God**, out of pure grace, has infused into our humanity and through which He has reconciled us in Him. Also, how the soul has so completely forgotten the covenant of **Holy Baptism** (in which it promised faith and loyalty to its Savior) and has so entirely defiled and darkened its righteousness (which **God** gave to it in Christ out of grace) through sins, that it now stands before **God’s** face in the beautiful garment of Christ’s innocence—which it has stained—like a filthy, torn, and ragged **swineherd** <note>This is a reference to the Parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15), who becomes a swineherd after squandering his inheritance.</note>, who has continually devoured the husks of vanity with the devil's swine, and is not worthy to be called a son of the Father or a member of Christ.

4. Fourthly, one should earnestly consider that fierce Death waits for him every hour and moment, and intends to seize him in this swineherd’s clothing in the midst of his sins and abominations, and plunge him into the abyss of hell as a perjurer and faith-breaker, who shall be kept for the judgment of **God** in the dark chamber of death.

5. Fifthly, one should consider the earnest and strict judgment of **God**, where he shall be placed alive with his abominations before the judgment; and all those whom he has offended here with words and deeds, or caused to do evil so that they also worked sin through his impulse, will step before his eyes and curse him, even in the sight of Christ and before all holy angels and people. And one should consider how he will stand there in great shame and mockery, as well as in great terror and eternal despair; and how he would eternally regret that for the sake of such a short time of **pleasure** <note>German: *Wollust*—this refers to worldly or carnal delight and physical gratification.</note> he has trifled away such a great eternal salvation, and did not take better care of himself so that he might also be among the communion of the saints and enjoy the eternal light and Divine power.

6. Sixthly, one should consider how the godless person loses his noble image (as **God** created him in His likeness) and receives a misshapen **mask** <note>original: "Larva." In Böhme's thought, the "larva" is a monstrous, non-human spiritual form that the soul takes on when it turns away from God's light.</note>, like a hellish worm or an abominable beast; and how he then becomes an enemy of **God**, against heaven and all holy angels and people; and how his companionhsip is eternally in the cruel darkness among the devils and hellish worms.

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the process of repentance. The previous page ended with the soul expressing blindness and unworthiness; here, the author addresses the reader directly about the trials of the "Christian resolve."</meta>

# 1. On True Repentance.

## 21.
To the dear reader who possesses a Christian **resolve** <term>resolve: "Fürsaß," a firm inner determination or spiritual commitment</term>, I will not hide how it commonly tends to go in such a difficult undertaking. To be sure, it happens differently for one person than for another, depending on how earnest and great the resolve is; for the Spirit of GOD is unconstrained and is accustomed to following various processes, as He knows each individual. However, he who has been in the war can speak of the battle, should it happen to another in the same way, for their instruction.

## 22.
It happens that such a heart, with a strict resolve, comes before GOD and enters into repentance. But it goes for them as it did for the **Canaanite woman** <note>In Matthew 15, Jesus initially ignores the Canaanite woman's pleas to test her faith; Böhme uses this to describe the "silence" of God during early prayer</note>, as if GOD did not want to hear. The heart remains without comfort, and their sins and unworthiness still appear before their eyes as if they were not worthy. The mind feels as though it were mute; the soul groans in the depths; the heart receives nothing and cannot even pour out its confession before GOD, just as if the heart and soul were locked away. The soul would gladly do so, but the flesh holds it captive. The devil covers it up tightly and models the way of **vanity** <term>vanity: "Eitelkeit," referring here to the hollow, temporary, and distracting nature of the material world</term> before the person again. He tickles them with the lusts of the flesh and says in the mind: "Wait a while; do this and that first; gather money for yourself beforehand so that you do not need the world, and then enter into a godly life and into repentance; there is time enough."

## 23.
Oh, how many hundreds perish in such a beginning when they enter back into vanity! It happens to them as it does to a **young graft** <note>original: "Pfröpflein." A horticultural metaphor for a newly planted spiritual life</note> that is broken off by the winds or withered by the heat.

## 24.
Listen, dear soul: if you wish to become a knight over death and hell in your Savior Christ, and if you wish for your young graft to become a tree and grow in the kingdom of Christ, then you must remain standing in your first earnest resolve. It will cost you your first paternal inheritance—indeed, your body and soul. You will be either an angel in GOD or a devil in hell. If you wish to be crowned, you must fight; you must conquer in Christ and not lie defeated beneath the devil. Your resolve must stand firm; you must not prefer temporal honor and goods over this.

## 25.
When the spirit of the flesh says, "Wait a while, it is not convenient right now," the soul must say: "Now is my time and hour to enter back into my **homeland** <note>original: "Vaterland." In Böhme’s mysticism, this refers to the divine realm or the original state of humanity before the Fall</note>."

26. Dear soul, this requires earnestness; it must not be merely a recitation of such words. The earnest, intended will must drive it, or it will not be attained. For if the soul wishes to attain Christ’s <term>Knight’s Wreath: "Ritter-Kränzlein," a symbolic crown of spiritual victory and honor</term> from the noble <term>Virgin Sophia: personified Divine Wisdom, often depicted by Böhme as the soul's heavenly bride</term>, it must woo her with a great desire of love. 27. # 1. Of True Repentance.

Thus it also happens to the soul, because it is still surrounded by the house of sin, so that, if it should fall again, its crown would not be defiled. ### The Process.

28. For this, a sober mind is required, which—with earnest resolve and in the highest humility, with repentance for its sins—should step before **GOD** in such a way that a resolve dwells within: that the person no longer wishes to walk in the old footsteps of vanity <term>vanity: "Eitelkeit," referring to the hollow, fleeting nature of the material world</term>. And even if the whole world should consider him a fool for it, or if he should lose honor and property, as well as this temporal life, he would nonetheless persevere in it.

29. Such a vow he must make to the noble Virgin Sophia <term>Virgin Sophia: personified Divine Wisdom, whom the author views as the soul's true celestial bride</term> in his resolve and mind, if he wishes to attain her marriage and love. For Christ also said: "Whoever does not leave wife, children, brothers, sisters, money, property, and all that he has, yes, even his earthly life, and follows me, is not worthy of me." Christ intends this for the soul’s disposition: that if there were anything which would hold the mind back in this matter, however beautiful and glorious it might seem in this world, the mind should regard it as nothing, and would rather choose to do without it than lose the love of the noble Virgin Sophia in the growth of the flower of Christ, in His tender humanity within us, according to heavenly corporeality. For this is the Rose of Sharon and the lily of the valley <note>original: "Rose im Thal," likely a reference to the Song of Solomon 2:1</note> of which Solomon plays, calling her his dear beloved and his chaste virgin, whom he loved so much, just as all the saints before and after him have ever loved her. Whoever has attained her has called her his pearl. A brief guide follows here on how one should pray for this; but the work itself is entrusted to the **Holy Spirit** in every heart where she is sought; He Himself forms the prayer within it.

### Warning to the Reader.

31. With good intentions, I will not hide from you, dear reader, what has been earnestly shown to me here: If you are still comfortable in the empty pleasures of the flesh, and are not in earnest purpose on the way to the new rebirth <term>Rebirth: A central concept for Böhme where the soul undergoes a radical internal transformation to restore the divine image lost in the Fall</term>, intending to become a different person, then leave the words written above in this prayer unspoken. Otherwise, they will become a judgment of **GOD** within you. You shall not misuse the holy names of **GOD**; be faithfully warned, for they belong to the needy soul; if she is truly in earnest, she will experience what they are.

### Instruction on how the soul should meet her dear Beloved, when He knocks at the Center, in the locked chamber of the soul.

32. Dear soul, it must be in earnest, without ceasing. You may well obtain the love of a kiss from the noble Sophia <note>Sophia, or Divine Wisdom, is portrayed by Böhme as the soul's heavenly bride and the feminine mirror of God. She represents the purity man lost at the Fall.</note> in the holy name of **JESUS**, for she stands even now before the soul's door and knocks, and warns the sinner of his godless way. If he then once desires her love in this way, she is willing to grant it and kisses him with the rays of her sweet love, from which the heart receives joy; but she does not immediately lie down in the marriage bed with the soul—that is, she does not immediately awaken the faded heavenly image <note>Böhme believed that Adam's fall caused a "fading" of a literal spiritual body or image, which must be "re-enlivened" through Christ.</note>, which faded in Paradise, within herself. There is danger for the human being; for if Adam and Lucifer fell, it may well still happen to man, because he still stands so strongly bound in vanity.

33. There must be a faithful bond of your promise if she is to crown you; you must first be tested. She takes her rays of love back from you and sees whether you will remain faithful; she may even let you plead and not answer you with a glance of her love. For if she is to crown you, you must first be judged, so that you taste the sour beer <note>original: "saure Bier"; a metaphor for the bitter consequences of one's sins and the "dregs" of a life lived apart from God.</note> which you have poured for yourself in your abominations. You must first go before the gates of hell, and [achieve] your victory, for...

Do not leave me in this distress; I am indeed guilty of the sins which now rise up in my conscience; if you abandon me, I must sink. You have promised me in your Word: even if a mother were to forget her child—which would be a painful thing—yet you will not forget me. I, a poor human, caught in your wrath, can do nothing now before you; I only immerse myself in your wounds and death.

O great mercy of God, deliver me from the devil’s bonds! I have no other refuge in anything but only in your holy wounds and death. In you I immerse myself in the anguish of my conscience; do with me as you will. In you I wish now to live or die, as you will; let me only die and pass away in your death; bury me only in your death, so that the anguish of hell may not touch me. For you have given his anguish to me and drowned your wrath in Him. 45. When the cornerstone, Christ <term>cornerstone: a biblical metaphor for Christ as the essential foundation of faith and the spiritual life</term>, stirs within the faded image of man during his heartfelt conversion and repentance, then Maiden Sophia <note>Sophia: representing Divine Wisdom, often personified in mystical literature as a celestial bride who reunites with the human soul</note> appears in the movement of Christ's Spirit. She appears before the soul in its faded state, dressed in her virginal adornment. At the sight of her, the soul is terrified by its own impurity, so that all its sins first wake up within it and tremble with fear before her. For here the judgment upon the soul's sin begins, so that the soul shrinks back in its unworthiness and feels ashamed before its beautiful beloved <note>original: "Buhlen"; in this mystical context, it refers to a spiritual lover or paramour rather than having a negative connotation</note>. The soul withdraws into itself and regards itself as nothing, feeling entirely unworthy to receive such a jewel <note>original: "Kleinod"; a precious treasure or gem</note>; this is understood by our own people who have tasted this jewel, and is known to no one else. But the noble Sophia approaches within the soul's essence and kisses it kindly, and tinctures <term>tincturing: a term borrowed from alchemy, here meaning to spiritually transform or "dye" the soul's dark, fiery nature with the light of divine love</term> the dark fire of the soul with her rays of love. She shines through the soul with her kiss of love, so that the soul leaps within its body for great joy. In the power of this virginal love, the soul rises up, triumphs, and praises the great **God** through the power of the noble Sophia.

I wish to provide a brief indication here of how it happens when the bride embraces the bridegroom. This is for the reflection of the reader who perhaps has not yet reached this state, to see if he might desire to follow after us and also join the dance where one plays with Sophia.

### To the Reader.

52. Dear reader, do not consider this to be some uncertain poem; it is the true foundation and contains within it the whole of Holy Scripture. For the "Book of Life" of Jesus Christ is clearly depicted here before your eyes, just as it was recognized by the author himself, for it was his own process <note>Böhme uses the word "Proceß" to describe a spiritual or alchemical transformation of the self</note>. He gives you the best that he has; may God grant the increase! A heavy judgment has been recognized against anyone who scoffs at this work. Let him be warned.

## A Little Morning Prayer, to be said upon rising, to commend oneself to God before letting anything else into oneself.

53. May God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit prevail. You alone, the true God! I thank You through Jesus Christ (Your dear Son) our Lord and Savior, for Your protection and shield, and for every benefit <note>original: "Wohlthat"</note>. I now commend myself—body and soul, and all that You have set me to work within my calling—into Your protection and shield. Be You the beginning of my thinking, seeking, striving, and all my doing. Work within me, so that I may begin everything to the praise of Your name and complete it in Your love for the service of my neighbor. Send Your good angel with me, that he may turn away from me the poisonous rays <note>Böhme often uses quasi-physical terms like "rays" to describe spiritual influences</note> of the devil and of corrupted nature. Guard me against the desire of all evil people. Soften <note>original: "Gütige"; to make well-disposed or kind</note> all my enemies before my face, and lead my spirit into Your vineyard, that I may labor and work therein in my office and calling as Your obedient servant (or handmaid), and bless me and everything I work with and handle with the blessing of Your love and mercy. Keep Your grace and love in Jesus Christ in and over me, and give me a joyful spirit to practice Your wonders. May Your Holy Spirit rule me from my beginning until my final end, and be within me the "willing, the working, and the accomplishing," Amen.

## ON REPENTANCE. Book 2. <note>original: "DE POENITENTIA. Lib. 2."</note>
->Or<-
# Of True Repentance,
### the 2nd Little Book.

A brief indication of the key to the understanding of Divine mysteries, how man may attain within himself to Divine contemplation <term>Beschaulichkeit: Böhme uses this to mean a state of mystical vision where one "beholds" the inner workings of God</term>.

->Written on February 9, 1623.<-

->Summaries.<-

Man should take a serious intent, §. 1. examine himself, 2. and contemplate his will. 3-6. If he feels the desire for conversion, it is God's voice. 7. Accordingly, he should examine his life in light of God's commandments, 8. so that he may see which image <note>Böhme refers to the "image" of the soul, which can either reflect God or a distorted animalistic/demonic nature</note> is within him; 9. thus he will find a beast and a devil within himself. 10. Thereupon he must immediately strive to go out from the animalistic will, 11. and take Christ's promise into his heart and pray. 12. He should despair of his own ability, but not of God's grace, 13. but rather remain hanging fast to Christ's promise, 14. and set his will firmly, praying constantly; 15. thus he will perceive powers, 16. and come worthily to the Marriage of the Lamb <note>A reference to the union of the soul with Christ, as described in the Book of Revelation</note>. 17. 18.

Whichever person wishes to attain to Divine contemplation within himself, and to speak with God in Christ, let him follow this process <note>Böhme uses "Proceß" to describe a structured spiritual or alchemical-like transformation of the self</note>, and he shall reach it.

# IX. The Way to Christ.

1. He should gather all his senses and reason, along with all imagination, together into one focus, and adopt such a strong internal visualization to contemplate himself, [to see] what he is: Since the Scripture calls him **God’s Image**, Gen. 1: 27, indeed a **temple of the Holy Spirit**, 1 Cor. 6: 19, who dwells within him; and calls him a member of Christ, and offers him Christ’s flesh and blood as food and drink.

2. Thus he should observe himself in his life, [to see] whether he is worthy of this great grace, and capable of this high title of "Christ," and begin to contemplate his entire life—what he has done, and how he has spent his whole time? Whether he finds himself in Christ? Whether he stands in the Divine Will, or toward what he is inclined? Whether he finds any will within himself that heartily longs for God and would gladly be saved?

3. And if he now finds a deeply-hidden will within himself that would gladly turn toward God’s grace if it only could; then let him know that this same will is the engrafted Word of God, spoken into [humanity] in Paradise after sin was committed; [know] that God Jehovah <note>The Hebrew name for God, used here to emphasize the Father's role as the eternal source</note>, as the Father, then draws him toward Christ: for in our own selfhood <term>Eigenheit: Böhme’s term for the fallen, self-centered nature that acts only for itself and is separated from God’s unity</term> we no longer have any will toward obedience.

4. But this same "drawing" of the Father, as the engrafted, spoken-in grace, draws all people—even the most godless (provided he is not a complete thistle <note>Böhme uses the "thistle" as a symbol for a person who has become so hardened and prickly with malice that they are unreceptive to God’s influence</note>, and is willing to stand still for a moment before that drawing) away from his false activity.

5. So that no person has cause to doubt God’s grace, as long as he finds within himself a desire to eventually be converted.

6. Let him not delay for a single moment more, as it is written: 
> **Today when you hear the Lord’s voice, do not harden your ears and hearts.**

7. For the desire for a once-and-for-all conversion is God’s voice in man, which the devil covers and holds back with his introduced images <note>Mental distractions or worldly idols that the devil uses to clutter the mind</note>, so that it is postponed from one day and year to the next, until finally the soul becomes a thistle and can no longer reach grace.

8. This person should do only this thing in his (sensory) contemplation: look at his whole course of life and hold it against the Ten Commandments of God, and against the love of the Gospel, which commands him to love his neighbor as himself, and that

# 1. Of True Repentance.

that he alone in Christ’s love is a child of grace; and let him see how far he has stepped away from it, and what his daily practice and desire is: Thus that same drawing of the Father will lead him into God’s righteousness, and show him the ingrained images in his heart, which he has loved instead of God, which he has held for his best treasure, and still holds.

9. These images will be: (1.) **Pride**—to love oneself and want to be honored by others. Likewise, it will be an image of power and force in his pride, wanting to rise in honor above others. (2.) Likewise, it will be the image of a **sow**, namely **Greed**, which wants to have everything for itself: even if it had the world and the heavens, it would also want to rule hell; one who desires more than is needed for this temporal life, and has no faith in God within him, but is a filthy sow that desires to pull everything into itself. (3.) Likewise, there will be in him an image of **Envy**, which stabs into other hearts and begrudges others if they have more temporal goods and honors than he. (4.) Likewise, it will be **Anger**, where envy rises up within like a poison, and for the slightest cause wants to push, strike, rage, and justify itself. (5.) Likewise, there will be drunkenness—indeed, many hundreds of earthly animals within him that he loves; for he loves everything in the world and has put it in Christ’s place, and honors it more than God. Let him only look at his words: how his mouth secretly slanders other people and causes trouble among his own, often repeating rumors without a clear conscience, rejoicing in a neighbor’s misfortune and wishing it upon him; all of which are the claws and talons <note>original: "Klauen und Krelle"</note> of the devil, and the image of the serpent that he carries within himself.

10. Now, let him examine these against God’s Word in the Law and the **Gospel** <note>original: "Evangelio"</note>; then he will see that he is more an animal and a devil than a true human being. He will clearly see how these ingrained and inherited images from God’s kingdom hinder him and lead him away: so that often, even when he would gladly repent and turn toward God, these devil-claws hold him back and lead him astray. These **masks** <note>original: "Larven" — Böhme uses this to describe false appearances or "idols" that cover the soul's true nature</note> trick the poor soul into imagining they are holiness, so that it enters into their pleasure once more, remains sitting in God’s wrath, and finally steps into the abyss when grace and the drawing of the Father fade away.

### IX. Way to Christ.

<meta>catchword: tes</meta>

11. To such a person we describe our own process: that as soon as he becomes aware of these **animals**, he should in that same hour and minute take hold of his soul and bring it into a single will—that he wishes to depart from the <term>animalistic will</term> <note>Böhme refers to the base, ego-driven desires—pride, greed, envy, and anger—as "animalistic" or "bestial" wills that distract from the divine.</note> and turn toward God through true <term>repentance</term> <note>original: "Busse." In this context, it implies a total internal transformation and a "turning around" of the soul’s orientation.</note>. And if he is not able to do this by his own strength or power, he should take into himself Christ’s <term>promise</term>, where Christ said: "Seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you. No son asks his father for bread and receives a stone; or for an egg and receives a scorpion. If you, then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will my Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him." (Luke 11: 13).

12. He should form this <term>promise</term> in his heart; for it is poison and death to the devil and to all the "animals" that have been worshipped and modeled within him. Let him come in that same hour before God with these internal, promised words in his prayer. He should first imagine all the hideous animals that he himself is, thinking of nothing else but that he is the filthy **swineherd** who has squandered all his Father’s goods and his rights as a child with the "swine" of the world and with these evil animals. He stands now before God’s face as nothing but a miserable, naked, ragged swineherd who has prostituted and squandered his Father's inheritance on the animalistic images of the world. He has no further right to God’s grace, nor is he worthy of it, much less to be called a Christian or a child of God. He should also despair of all the good works he has ever done, for they proceeded only from a hypocritical appearance of **godliness**, through which the "human-devil" <note>A term Böhme uses for the false, self-righteous ego that pretends to be holy while remaining trapped in pride.</note> wishes to be called an angel. For "without **faith** it is impossible to please God," says the Scripture.

13. But he must not despair of Divine Grace—only of himself and his own ability and power—and he must bow down in his soul with all his might before God. And even if his heart speaks a loud "No," or says, "Wait longer, today is not a good time," or "Your sins are too great, it is impossible for you to come into God’s favor," so that he becomes so anxious within himself that he cannot pray to God, receiving neither comfort nor strength in his heart, feeling as if his soul were entirely blind and dead to God—yet he should stand firm, and God—

And although he may consider himself too unworthy—feeling like a stranger who no longer deserves the inheritance of Christ and has lost his rights—he should nevertheless firmly fix in his mind that Christ said: *He came to seek and save that which is lost*, meaning the poor, blind sinner who is dead to God. He should form this <term>promise</term> <note>original: "Verheissung." For Böhme, a divine promise is not just a statement but an active power that the soul must "model" or "form" within itself.</note> within himself and make such a stern resolution that he will not depart from the promised grace of God in Christ, even if his body and soul should break apart. And even if he should never obtain comfort or the feeling of forgiveness in his heart for his entire life, God's promise is still more steadfast than any comfort he might ever experience.

15. He should also resolve, and lock his will so firmly into this purpose, that he will no longer enter into those old **animalistic images** and vices, even if all his "swine" and "beasts" should mourn for their shepherd. Even if he must be seen as a **fool** by all the world for doing so, he must remain constant in his purpose and in God's promise of grace. If he is a child of death, let him be within Christ's promise in Christ's death, and die and live to Him as He wills. He should only direct his purpose into constant prayer and sighing to God, surrendering all his beginnings and deeds into the works of God's hands, and become still and quiet from the internal "modeling" of <term>greed, envy, and pride</term> <note>These "three animals" are the primary vices Böhme identifies as blocking the soul from God.</note>. If he only surrenders these three animals, the others will very soon begin to grow weak and sick, and draw near to death. For Christ will soon take a **form** unto life within those promised words which the man forms in his mind and wraps himself in; Christ will begin to work in him, whereby his prayer will become more powerful, and he will (more and more) be strengthened in the spirit of grace.

16. Just as a seed works toward becoming a child in the **mother's womb**, growing through many shocks of nature and external accidents until the child receives its life; so it also happens here. The more the human "goes out" from his own images <note>In Böhme’s thought, "going out" means denying the ego and the mental constructs of worldly desire.</note>, the more he "enters into" God, until at last Christ becomes liv[ing] in the embodied grace.

### IX. The Way to Christ.

...becomes alive, which happens in great earnestness of purpose; so immediately the marriage with **Lady Sophia** <term>Sophia</term> <note>In Böhme’s mystical theology, Sophia represents Divine Wisdom, the eternal "bride" of the soul who was lost at the Fall and is rediscovered through spiritual rebirth.</note> begins, where the two loves receive each other with joy, and with very inward desire penetrate into the most sweet love of God together: there, in a short time, the **Marriage of the Lamb** is prepared, where Lady Sophia (as the worthy humanity of Christ) is wedded with the soul. Luke 15: 7.

17. Regarding this, we have neither pen nor words to write or to speak of what the sweet grace of God in Christ's humanity may be, and what may happen to those who worthily come to the Marriage of the Lamb; which we have experienced ourselves in our own <term>process</term> <note>Böhme uses "process" to describe the organic, step-by-step transformation of the soul from a state of wrath to a state of light.</note> and know that we have a true foundation for our writing: which we would most heartily wish to share with our brothers in the love of Christ. If it were possible that they would believe our faithful, childlike counsel, they would experience within themselves that from which this **simple hand** <note>A self-deprecating reference to himself as an uneducated shoemaker; he emphasizes that his insights come from divine revelation rather than academic learning.</note> understands and knows these great mysteries.

18. Since we have previously written a quite detailed treatise on **Repentance and the New Rebirth**, we will let it remain here as only an indication, and refer the reader there, as well as to the great work on Genesis: * There he will find the entire foundation of whatever he might wish to ask, in sufficient detail; and we exhort him in a Christian manner to follow after us in this process, so he will come to **Divine Contemplation** within himself, and hear what the Lord says through Christ in him. And herewith we commend him to the love of Christ.

11. Dear Christian reader, you should well consider what prayer is and why God bids us to pray. It is not like stepping before a worldly king or lord when one has offended him and asking him for grace, while often thinking quite differently in one’s heart. No: rather, it is an **outgoing of oneself**, in which a person surrenders themselves to God with all their powers, with all that they are, and all that they possess. Indeed, through true prayer, one surrenders oneself to be the very property of God. He returns with the **prodigal son** <note>Reference to the Parable of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15, representing the soul's return to God.</note> to the Father, into his first fatherland and inheritance from which Adam, our first father, led him out. He no longer has any <term>natural right: (Natur-Recht), the legal or inherent claim to heavenly status that humanity possessed before the Fall.</term> to heavenly goods; he lost them all with Adam’s departure and consumed them through his dalliance with the devil in vanity.

He must deem himself entirely unworthy of all heavenly goods by natural right and fall down before God his heavenly Father, asking for the offered mercy in His son Jesus Christ: that He would be pleased to accept him again as a day-laborer and worker in His vineyard, and would give him again heavenly food and drink for his languishing, hungry, and thirsty soul. He prays that he might no longer have to eat the husks of vanity, lies, and falsehood with the devil’s swine, and thus perish in unbelief without heavenly power. Thus, the poor, hungry soul will powerfully and **substantially** <note>In this context, "substantially" (wesentlich) implies that the grace is not just a concept, but a real, spiritual substance that feeds the soul.</note> receive within itself that which it asks and desires from God—namely, the flesh and blood of Jesus Christ, its Savior, which is offered out of grace to all hungry, penitent souls.

He falls upon the neck of the soul's **essence of life** <note>original: "Eſſentz des Lebens." There, the **signet ring**—the precious testament of God’s covenant in the blood of Jesus Christ—is placed upon the soul once more, and through such a covenant and sealing, the soul is accepted again as a child of God.

15. Therefore, I tell the Christian reader this: prayer is not merely **lip service** <note>original: "Mund-Werck," literally "mouth-work." The author emphasizes that true prayer must be an internal transformation, not just spoken words.</note>, like when one stands before a worldly lord to ask for temporal things or for a debt to be forgiven. God does not bid us ask only for external **imputed grace** <note>original: "zugerechnete Gnade." This refers to the theological idea of being declared righteous legally; the author contrasts this with a grace that actually changes the person's nature.</note>, but for childlike, **actual grace**, where the Holy Spirit Himself asks and prays within us through the merit of Christ. In this way, He makes grace powerful within us, and through this working, He also blots out sin in us, drowning it in Christ’s death and destroying hell. Through Christ's payment, He raises the gates of eternal life within us through <note>meaning: "out of" or "amidst"</note> God's wrath, strips the devil of his power over us, and clothes us in Christ. Thus, in the spirit and merit of Christ, we cry out to the Father of all mercy: **Abba, dear Father** <note>original: "Abba." An Aramaic term for "Father" or "Daddy," expressing the most intimate possible relationship between the believer and God.</note>.

16. Then Saint Paul says: we have not received a spirit of servitude, that we must fear again, but a childlike spirit <note>original: "kindlichen Geist." This refers to the "spirit of adoption" mentioned in Romans 8:15, emphasizing a relationship of a child to a father rather than a slave to a master.</note>, so that we may ask the Father with a joyful heart and with all confidence, and He will give it to us. 17. For the sake of giving and receiving, God tells us to ask and pray, as Christ says: My Father will give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him for it. Also: Ask, and you shall receive; seek, and you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you. (Luke 11: 9–13).

18. Every prayer that does not find and receive is cold and lukewarm, and is stuck in a hindrance of temporal, earthly things. That is to say: the soul does not approach God purely; it does not want to surrender itself entirely to God, but still clings to earthly love, which holds it captive so that it cannot reach God’s dwelling place.

19. If one wishes to pray rightly, one should turn away from every **creature** <note>In this context, "creature" (Creatur) refers to anything created—worldly objects, people, or selfish desires—that distracts the soul from the Creator.</note> and step before God purely with the will and the mind. There must be such a purpose and earnestness, like that of the poor tax collector in the temple, and like the **prodigal son**, who come to God in this way. And even though **reason** <note>original: "Vernunft." Böhme often uses this term to describe human logic or the rational mind, which he believes often stands in the way of spiritual faith.</note> speaks within flesh and blood, saying "No, you will not be heard; your sins are too great," or, "it is not the right time, wait longer," or "do this or that first so that you have leisure and time for it afterward," or says: "Why do you pray? You cannot come before God with your desire anyway, for you receive no power within yourself"—do not let this confuse you. The power is in the **inner ground** <note>original: "inwendigen Grunde." This is a central term in German mysticism referring to the deepest, most essential part of the soul where God dwells.</note>, in the desire of the will, and it works with God. Just stand still and wait for the Lord; it will finally break through so that you will feel it in your heart and thank God.

20. Whoever wishes to pray rightly and reach God’s power and Spirit with their desire should forgive all their enemies and include them in their prayer, asking God that He would also convert them and reconcile them with Him in His love. This is so that no **serpent** <note>A metaphor for malice or lingering resentment that poisons the spiritual process.</note> remains in the heart to hold the soul back and tear the power of prayer away from it, as Christ says: The devil tears the word from their hearts, so that they do not believe and are not saved. [If you are] offering [at the] altar, and you remember there that your brother has something against you, go your way first and be reconciled with your brother; then come and offer your gift. (Matt. 5:23, 24.) Likewise <note>original: "Item," a Latin term commonly used in early modern German to mean "similarly" or "also."</note> in the Lord's Prayer: Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. (Matt. 6:12.) [This is] so that the evil enemy does not tempt us with ingrained hatred, nor hinder us or lead us into doubt.

21. God demands a pure, bare, and naked soul in prayer: although it may be surrounded by vanity, its will should come purely before God, so that He may begin to work in its will, and thereafter daily kill the vanity of the flesh. Thus, the will should certainly be directed toward God with desire, so that it says with Jacob, when he wrestled with God the whole night: Lord, I will not let you go unless You bless me. (Gen. 32:26.)

22. And even if the heart palpitates <note>original: "zappelt," which can mean to fidget or struggle; here it refers to the heart’s trembling or unrest during spiritual struggle.</note> and doubts, and all sorts of hindrances occur, the will should nevertheless remain standing, and firmly imagine <term>einbilden|The process by which the soul fixes its internal focus or "forms" itself into a specific spiritual state; for Böhme, the "imagination" is a creative power of the soul.</term> grace within itself, and not wish to let go of it. And even if the devil swings the lust of the flesh upward, making the soul terrified and thinking it has been cast off by God, the will should nevertheless hang onto grace like a child at its mother’s breasts, and constantly fight against the devil and his desire in flesh and blood until it finally triumphs and overcomes the devil in the Spirit of Christ; then it will see and perceive great wonders within itself, and will recognize that it is true: there is such great joy in heaven over the converted soul, more than over ninety-nine righteous ones who do not need such repentance. (Luke 15:7.)

23. Therefore, whoever wishes to pray rightly should firmly impress upon himself that he wishes to come to Divine grace and favor, and will certainly obtain that which he asks. Therefore, his prayer should also be so directed that it does not run against God’s order: but he should think that in his prayer he wishes to work with God; just as the wood on the tree works with the tree's power, so also should he desire to work only with God's power and will; otherwise, his prayer is only a working in the shells <note>original: "Schalen," referring to the outer husks or bark of the tree, signifying superficiality versus the "inner" sap of the Spirit.</note> of the true Tree of Life: for he then works only outwardly in the elements, and not inwardly with and in God.

...so that he becomes fiery and truly desirous: In which desire God Himself works; Then man speaks rightly with God, and God speaks effectively with the soul of man.

31. <note>The previous page ended with the beginning of the word "shine" (leuchte).</note> ...shine then once more within my outer light of the sun and moon, so that I may learn to recognize your inward power through the outer essence.

O you super-luminous light of the great hiddenness, grant me the rays of your hidden holiness, so that in my own light I may see the light of your radiance!

O you fire and light of the great inwardness, have mercy on my misery, and help me out of this dark house in which I am imprisoned. Grant me once again a true knowledge of your essence, for which you originally formed the <term>mind (Gemüthe) <note>In Böhme’s writing, the "Gemüthe" is more than just the intellect; it is the "soul-mind," the seat of the will and the center of human consciousness where the divine and the natural meet.</note></term> in nature, and which you ordained to be the will of your figures and creatures: Lead me back into my former glory through Christ my Savior.

And although the body in this time is not worthy of it, because it has become a stinking <note>original: "Cadaver" (Latin for corpse). 17th-century spiritual writers often used this term to emphasize the corruption of the physical body following the Fall of Man.</note> corpse: yet shine through my noble mind, as your image, and let it dwell in heaven, in Christ my Savior, in the fellowship of your holy angels.

Place it in the midday of your wonders, for which you have formed it, and rule, O Lord Jesus Christ, as with your inheritance, through it over all things. And help me to be humble, and not to take credit for what you do, but to look to you, so that my desire may praise you, and that I may live constantly in your harmony, and desire to begin or do nothing without you.

O Lord, you most holy light, let my mind dwell in your courtyards, that it may rejoice in your luster which flows out from you, and never depart from you again: But lead it back to the fellowship of the holy angels, for which you have ordained it.

O Holy Name Immanuel <note>Hebrew for "God with us."</note>, it is yours; do with it what you will, Amen.

Instead, you desire that we speak, will, and form with you, under penalty of eternal punishment, as your commandment sounds: 
> Cursed be he who does not keep all the words of this law. (Deuteronomy 27:26.)

O great GOD! what shall I now say here before you? How uncountably often do we lead your Word and power in our mouths into false formation, when we swear by your name, curse, introduce false lust into it, and make a beautiful, glistering image on our lips and talk each other into it as truth—and yet inside it is nothing but a serpent full of lies and poison. And thus, we form your Word into a serpent and a devilish image under a righteous appearance.

## The 3rd Commandment.

54 **Remember the Sabbath day, that you keep it holy, etc. (For in six days the Lord created heaven and earth, and the sea, and all that is in them, and rested on the seventh day. (Exodus 20: 8-11.)**

### Prayer.

> **Dear God!** this commandment reminds me of my inward, right, Divine rest in your love and power; That my will should rest in you from its own pleasantness of self-will <note>The author uses "self-will" (eigenes Willen) to describe the human ego's desire to act independently of God's guidance.</note>, and you, eternal **God**, would work with your power in my will: You are the right **Sabbath**, in whom all my powers should work in an eternal rest and be and remain holy in you.

> **O alas!** it was the true **Paradise**, into which you placed our first parents, that they should keep your **Sabbath** holy as your indwelling, actual power—that is, to love it rightly—and introduce no foreign lust of false desire into it, and not darken this **Holy Sabbath** of your indwelling power with their own desire, nor introduce the serpent's cunning and falsehood into it; but rather to will, work, and live with you, so that you alone might be the working, willing, and doing within me.

...image <note>original: "Figur"; Böhme uses this to mean a spiritual representation or a model provided by God for human contemplation.</note> before me, in which I see your order and will: You demand of me the capacity to live in your order, in your will, as you created me in **Adam**; But my father Adam turned his will away from you, and introduced it into his own lust and desire, and led such **Paradisal working** in your rest into a fiery, hostile, proud, greedy, envious, and wrathful working, and has desecrated your and his **Sabbath**, and introduced the serpent's false working and willing into it. For which sake you have cast him out of such rest and Paradisal working, and cursed his false working; because he works with the devil and hell, and runs in pure unrest, so it is also an enmity against the **Holy Sabbath**.

You present to us in this commandment how you, in the six properties of eternal nature—being (1) the **desire**, (2) the **mobility**, (3) the **sensibility**, (4) the **fire** or **life**, (5) the **light of love**, (6) the **understanding** or **knowledge of the powers** <note>These "six properties" are a central part of Böhme’s complex mystical system describing how God manifests from the void into the physical and spiritual world.</note>—have worked all things, and have yet introduced it into the seventh property, as into the **essential unity and wisdom**, for rest, wherein all your works were to rest in your working love, wherein you wished to work with your love.

Which then was the true **Paradise on Earth** in the elements, where your poured-out love held the supreme rule in all. But the devil and man have corrupted this; therefore you, **righteous GOD**, have cursed the working of the individual's own false will, and withdrawn your Sabbath from it, so that now all things stand in pure misery and distress, in breaking, murder, killing, and strife. My father Adam has bequeathed such to me, so that I now work and run in your wrath, and constantly break and desecrate your Sabbath within me, and abuse your name, which has entered into my working and willing along with my life. But because man has become blind to such knowledge, you have presented to him in your commandments a figure and form for which you created him, and in which order he once stood; And you demand of him, that he should in such form and order keep the Sabbath holy.

God, establish a new Sabbath in us in Jesus Christ, and make your dwelling in us, and hallow again your formed Word <note>original: "gebildetes Wort"; this refers to the creative Word of God that takes shape within the human soul, restoring the divine image.</note> as our mind and soul, and place us into the eternal Sabbath, as into the rest of your unity.

Break then within me the devil's Sabbath and false working, and give me an obedient heart that constantly hungers for your Sabbath. And let your Word keep the Sabbath in me, so that my soul may hear what you speak through your working within me, so that it may be obedient to you, and I may place all my trust in you alone.

O you eternal Love, Jesus Christ! In your Sabbath I surrender myself entirely: Deliver me only from evil. Amen.

->Prayer.<-

O Eternal God, in our physical parents you present to us an image of our eternal Father and our eternal Mother: For you are our Father, from whom we have received our life; and your Word is our Mother, who has given us birth out of your creation and formed us according to the image of your revelation. Our soul and mind <note>original: "Gemüthe"; in this context, it refers to the seat of emotions, will, and spiritual perception, often translated as 'disposition' or 'heart.'</note> are, O God Father, your image, and our body is an image of your outgoing Word. This Word is our eternal Mother, in whose womb we are conceived and nourished: We should honor her, humble ourselves before her, and be obedient to her. Just as we should honor our external, physical parents, so also must we honor our Eternal parents, from whose foundation we have sprouted.

O eternal Father, we have become disobedient to you and have given ourselves over to the care of a foreign mother: We have accepted the World as our mother, and we have become faithless to the inward Mother—to your power within your Word. Now we must suck poison and death from the breasts of this foreign mother; yes, she now carries us in her body of adversity <note>original: "Wiederwärtigkeit"; in mystical theology, this refers to the state of conflict or "contrariety" found in the fallen material world.</note>, gives birth to us and consumes us again in your wrath, and nourishes us for the duration of this entire external life in sheer misery, sorrow, toil, and want, in suffering and poverty. She holds us captive within herself so that we cannot see our true eternal Mother; our soul laments for her, but your anger holds us imprisoned so that we must serve the foreign mother.

O God, how long will you forget us in our misery! Take us back again as your children, and give us birth anew in our eternal Mother, and give us an obedient will, so that we may never deviate from you again for all eternity.

Give us also an obedient heart toward our physical parents, that we may love and honor them as your established order, since you have given us birth through them into this world and to the light—

# The Third Little Book.
# ON EQUANIMITY <note>original Latin: "DE ÆQUANIMITATE"</note>,
### or
# Concerning True Resignation <note>original German: "Gelassenheit" — a central concept in German mysticism referring to a state of letting go, surrender to God, and stillness of the ego</note>.

### The 1st Chapter.

# IX. The Way to Christ.

...[whoever] works with Him in His being is one Spirit with Him. 43. But whatever works in selfhood <term>Selbheit: the state of being centered on one’s own ego or "self-will"</term> is outside of God's governance of Love. 44. All works of self-interest <term>Eigenheit: literally "own-ness," referring to actions taken for the sake of the ego</term> burn in the fire. 45. For selfhood works in the wrestling wheel of nature <note>A term Böhme uses to describe the turbulent, conflicting forces of existence before they are harmonized by divine light</note> toward God's judgment. 46. 47. But if a person turns back, the good will be released from the evil. 48.

We have a true example in Lucifer, and also in Adam, the first man, of what selfhood does when it receives the external light as its own property, so that it may walk in its own governance through the intellect. One can also see this in those learned in the arts <note>This refers to scholars and those possessing intellectual or academic knowledge</note>, when they obtain the light of external nature as a possession in their own reason, how nothing but pride <note>original German: "Hoffart"</note> arises from it. Yet the whole world seeks and desires this so intensely, as if it were the greatest treasure; and indeed, it is perhaps the best treasure of this world, if it is used correctly.

2. But because selfhood—acting as Reason—is caught in a heavy prison, namely in God's wrath as well as in worldliness, and stands firmly bound, it is very dangerous for a person to carry the light of knowledge within their selfhood as if it were the property of that selfhood.

3. For the wrath of eternal and temporal nature soon takes delight in this, causing selfhood and one's own reason to rise up in pride and break away from true, resigned humility toward God. It no longer wishes to eat from the fruit of Paradise, but rather from the quality of selfhood, as from the governance of life in which good and evil reside. This is what Lucifer and Adam did; both of them, through the desire of creaturely selfhood, went back into the original condition <note>original: "Urstand," the fundamental source of being</note> from which the creature was born and entered into a created form—Lucifer into the center of the wrathful nature, into the fire's matrix <term>Matrix: in Böhme's philosophy, a "womb" or generating principle from which things come into being</term>, and Adam into the earthly nature, into the matrix of the external world, into the desire for good and evil.

4. This happened to both of them because they had the light of understanding shining within their selfhood, in which they could mirror themselves and behold their own essence. Through this, the spirit of selfhood entered into the imagination <note>original: "Imagination" — Böhme uses this to mean the creative or formative power of the will to shape its own reality</note> as a desire for the center, seeking to exalt itself,

He warns that intellectual reason, when divorced from humility, leads to pride and spiritual imprisonment.</summary>

->### Chap. 1. Of True Gelassenheit.<-
<note>The German term "Gelassenheit" is central to Böhme’s thought; it implies a state of being "yielded," "resigned," or "surrendered" to the divine will, letting go of the ego.</note>

...[to ex]alt <note>The fragment "ben" likely completes the verb "erheben," meaning to exalt or raise up</note> themselves, becoming great and powerful, and moreover, to become more clever. For just as Lucifer sought the **Fire-Mother** <note>Böhme’s term for the energetic, harsh source-principle of nature from which all things arise</note> in his **Center**, and thereby intended to rule over God’s Love and the entire **Angelic Host**; so too Adam desired to test the **Mother**—from which Good and Evil flow—within his essence, and he directed his desire into her, with the will to become clever and understanding.

5. Both of these, Lucifer and Adam, were caught in the **Mother** through their false desire. They broke away from <term>Gelassenheit: yieldedness or surrender to God</term> and were trapped by their will-spirit and desire in the **Mother**, who immediately gained governance over the creature. Thus Lucifer remained in the fierce, dark torment of fire, and that same fire became manifest in his will-spirit, through which the creature, in its desire, became an enemy of God’s Love and Gentleness.

6. So also Adam was immediately seized by the **Earthly Mother**, which is both Good and Evil, created as a single being out of God’s Love and Wrath; and the earthly quality immediately gained governance in Adam. From this, it happened that heat and cold, envy, wrath, and all false ill-will and malice against God became manifest and dominant within him.

7. However, if they had not brought the light of knowledge into their **selfhood** <term>Selbheit: the state of being centered on one’s own ego</term>, then the mirror of knowledge of the **Center** and the original state of the creature would not have been revealed to them, from which **Imagination** <note>In this context, the formative power of the soul to "image" or create its own internal reality</note> and lust arose.

8. In the same way, this still brings danger today to the enlightened children of God. When the sun of the great vision of God’s holiness shines upon many, causing their life to step forth in triumph, **Reason** mirrors itself therein. The will then enters into **selfhood** as its own inquiry, wishing to test the **Center** from which the light shines, and to force itself into it through its own **selfhood**.

9. From this arises wretched pride and **self-conceit** <note>original: "Dünckel"</note>, so that one’s own **Reason** (which is yet only a mirror of the Eternal) thinks it is something more—that whatever it does, it is God’s will doing it through her, and that she is a prophetess. Yet she is only within herself, walking in her own desire, in which the **Center** of the creature soon soars—

# IX. Way to Christ.

...swings, and enters into its own desire of falsehood against God, so that the will enters into a **conceit** <note>German: *Dünckel*. Refers to intellectual pride or a deluded self-opinion.</note>.

10. So then the **Flattering-Devil** <note>original: "Schmeichel-Teufel." A personification of the temptation to feel spiritually superior or "special."</note> steps to him, and sifts the <term>Center: the inner energetic core of a being where spiritual forces interact</term> of the creature, and leads his false desire into it, so that the human becomes drunken in his **selfhood**, as if he were being driven by God. Thereby the good beginning, wherein the light of God was shining in the creature, is corrupted, and that same light of God departs from him.

11. Then the external light of outer nature remains shining in the creature, for its own **selfhood** swings into it, and so the soul thinks it is still the first light from God; but no, into this (as into the **conceit** of selfhood, into the outer **light of reason**) the devil swings himself back in with a sevenfold desire, after he was forced to yield from the first light, which is Divine. Of which Christ says: *When the unclean spirit departs from a man, he wanders through dry places, seeking rest, and finds none: Then he takes seven spirits to himself, who are worse than he, and returns again into his first house, and finds it swept and decorated, and dwells there then, and it becomes worse with that same man than before,* etc. <note>original: "mit Besemen geschmücket," literally "adorned with brooms," following the imagery of a house swept clean. Reference to Matthew 12:43-45.</note>

12. The decorated house is the **light of reason** in **selfhood**; for when a person leads his desire and will into God, and enters into the abstinence of his evil life, and desires God's love, then that love appears to him with its very friendly, joy-filled glance, by which also the outer light of reason is ignited. For where God's light is ignited, everything becomes light; there the devil cannot remain, he must depart from there. So then he searches through the <term>Primal Origin: the foundational state or source-spring of a being</term> of the **Mother of Life**, which is the **Center**; but it has become a dry, powerless place. The **Wrath of God**, as the center of nature, is in its own property entirely powerless, meager, and dry, and cannot come to governance. Satan searches through this place to see if he might find any gate open, where he could enter with his desire and sift the soul, so that it might exalt itself.

### Chapter 1. Section 3. On True Resignation.

13. When the **Light of Reason** <term>Vernunft-Licht: Intellectual knowledge or human logic used independently of divine revelation.</term> swings into the center—that is, into **Selfhood**—and enters into its own delusion, it departs from God’s light once again. Now the devil finds an open gate to him, and a beautifully decorated house (the Light of Reason) for his dwelling; thus he takes the seven forms of life's property <note>In Böhme’s theology, these are the seven foundational qualities or "source-spirits" of nature that can manifest as either heavenly or hellish.</note> into himself in Selfhood: like hypocrites who have departed from God and gone into Selfhood. There he enters and places his desire in the pleasure of Selfhood and false imagination, wherein the **Will-Spirit** sees itself within the forms of life’s properties in the external light. There he sinks into himself as if he were drunk; then the **Stars** <term>Gestirne: The astral or sidereal influences that Böhme believed governed the physical world and the rational mind.</term> seize him and lead their mighty constellation into it, seeking to find the wonders of God there and to reveal themselves within them. For every creature longs for God. And although the Stars cannot grasp the Spirit of God, they much prefer a house of light in which to delight themselves rather than a closed house where they have no support.

14. Thus this person goes about as if he had become drunk on the Stars; he perceives great and wondrous things and has a steady guide in the Stars. So the devil also notices quite well where a gate stands open for him, so that he may ignite the **Center of Life**, causing the Will-Spirit to soar upward in its own pride, in its **conceit** (or even in greed).

15. From this arises **self-honor**, so that the Will of Reason wants to be honored. For he thinks he has the **roast of salvation** <note>original: "Braten des Heils." A colorful idiom suggesting he believes he has "captured the prize" or secured the ultimate spiritual benefit through his own efforts.</note> because he possesses a Light of Reason, and he can judge the "closed house" <note>Referring to other people who may appear spiritually "unlit" or simpler in their faith.</note> which God may well unlock. He thinks honor is now due to him because he has attained rational understanding, and he never realizes how the devil delights himself with his desire in the seven life-forms of the center of nature, or what ghastly errors he brings about.

16. From this understanding, the **false Babel** <note>Referring to the biblical Tower of Babel, used here to represent the confusion and corruption Böhme saw in institutional churches that relied on human logic rather than the Holy Spirit.</note> was born in the Christian Church on earth, where men judge and rule by rational conclusions, and have placed upon it the **Child of Drunkenness**—along with selfhood and own-lust—well-adorned like a beautiful maiden.

17. But the devil has moved into the seven life-forms of the Center as his lodging, namely into the selfhood of the

# IX. Way to Christ.

17. ...his own reason, and leads his will and desire constantly into this decorated virgin assumed from the stars; He is her beast, upon which she rides elegantly adorned in her own forms of life (as can be seen in the *Apocalypse* <note>original: "Apocal."; a reference to the Whore of Babylon riding the beast in Revelation 17.</note>). Thus she has taken the external luster, as the light of reason, from God's holiness, and thinks she is the beautiful child in the house, but the devil is at home inside her.

18. And so it goes for all those who are once enlightened by God, but then depart from true resignation <term>Gelassenheit: A central concept in German mysticism referring to the state of "yieldedness" or surrendering one's will to God.</term>, and wean themselves from the true mother’s breasts, namely from right humility.

### The *Process* <term>Processus: A technical term for the systematic progression or "way" of spiritual development.</term> of a True Christian, and How He Should Walk.

19. Reason will give me pause and say: "It is surely right and good that a person of God also attains the light of outward nature and reason, so that he may govern his life wisely by the power of the Holy Scriptures."

20. Yes, it is right, and nothing more useful or better can happen to a person; whoever can attain and receive the light of God and the light of time <note>Böhme distinguishes between "the light of time" (temporal, rational knowledge) and "the light of God" (eternal, spiritual wisdom).</note> possesses a treasure above all the treasures of this world, for it is an eye for both time and eternity.

21. But hear how you should use it: The light of God opens itself first in the soul; it shines forth like the light from a candle, and immediately kindles the outer light of reason—not so that it should give itself over entirely to the dominion of reason as the outer man. No, the outer man views himself in that penetrating glow, like an image before a mirror; he immediately learns to know himself in his selfhood <term>Selbheit: The ego-driven state of viewing oneself as an independent, self-centered entity separate from God.</term>, which is good and useful for him.

22. When this happens, reason—as the creaturely selfhood—can do nothing better than to ensure it does not gaze upon itself in its own creaturely selfhood, and that it does not enter into the center with the will of desire and seek itself. Otherwise, it breaks itself off from God’s essence (which rises with the light of God, from which the soul should eat and be refreshed) and eats instead from the outer light and essence, thereby drawing the poison <note>original: "Gift"; in 17th-century German, this word specifically means poison or venom, suggesting that self-centered knowledge is spiritually toxic.</note> back into itself.

<summary>Böhme explains that while human reason is a valuable "light of time," it must remain subordinate to divine light; if reason seeks its own glory, it becomes a "beast" for the devil.</summary>

## Chapter 1. 3. On True Resignation.

23. The will of the creature <term>Creatur: Meaning the human being as a created entity.</term> should sink itself completely, with all its reason and desire, into itself as an unworthy child that is not at all deserving of these high graces. It should attribute no knowledge or understanding to itself, nor should it ask for or desire any understanding from God within its natural selfhood <term>Selbheit: The ego or the false sense of "self" that separates the soul from God.</term>. Instead, it should simply and innocently sink into the love and grace of God in Christ Jesus, desiring to be as if dead to its own reason and selfhood within the life of God, and give itself over entirely to the life of God in love, so that He may do with it as with His instrument—how and what He wills.

24. No shining light within the divine or human ground should be claimed by one’s own reason; one should want or desire nothing but God’s grace in Christ alone. Just as a child always longs only for the mother’s breasts, so too should the hunger [of the soul] constantly enter into God’s love and never allow itself to be broken away from such hunger. When the external reason triumphs in the light and says, "I have the true child," the will of desire should bow it to the earth and lead it into the highest humility and a holy lack of understanding <note>original: "albern Unverstand"; Böhme uses "albern" in its older sense of "simple" or "innocent," rather than "silly." It refers to a state of spiritual unknowing.</note>. It should say to the reason: "You are foolish and have nothing but God’s grace; you must wind yourself into that grace with great humility and become completely nothing within yourself. You must neither know nor love yourself; everything that is in and of you must be regarded as nothing, merely as an instrument of God. You must lead your desire into God’s mercy alone, departing from all self-owned knowledge and willing, holding it all as nothing, and never forming a will to enter into it again, whether near or far."

25. And when this happens, the natural will enters into its own impotence, and the devil is no longer able to fight against it with his false desires; for the places of his [the devil's] rest become completely dry and powerless to him.

26. Then the Holy Spirit from God takes possession of the life-form <term>Lebens-Gestältniß: The inner configuration or "shape" of a person's life and soul.</term> and raises up His governance; that is, He ignites the life-form with His flame of love. Then the high science and knowledge of the Center of all beings <note>original: "Centri aller Wesen"</note> arises, according to the inner and outer constellation <term>Constellation: A term from Böhme’s "spiritual physics" referring to the alignment of forces or qualities within a person.</term> of the creature, occurring in a subtle, driving fire with great delight.
