# IX. The Way to Christ.
<meta>catchword: Child</meta>

...desire to sink itself into that same light, and to consider itself unworthy and as nothing before it.

27. Thus, the soul’s own desire presses into the Nothing <note>Böhme’s "Nothing" (*Nichts*) is not a void, but the *Ungrund*: the divine source that exists before and beyond all created things.</note>, seeking only God’s working and doing—whatever He wills within it. Then the Spirit of God presses out through the desire of this yielded humility. In this way, the human selfhood <term>Selbheit: The ego or false sense of "self" that separates the soul from God.</term> follows after the Spirit of God in the trembling and joys of humility; and thus it may behold everything that is in time and eternity, for everything is near to it.

28. When the Spirit of God moves as a fire of the flame of love, then the will-spirit of the soul bows down and says: "Lord, let the honor be to Your name, and not to me; You have the power to take strength, power, might, wisdom, and knowledge. Do what You will; I know and can do nothing. I will go nowhere unless You lead me as Your instrument; do in and with me whatever You will."

29. In such humble, total surrender, the spark of Divine Power falls into the center of the life-formation <term>Lebens-Gestaltniß: The inner structure or vital configuration of a person's life and soul.</term>—like tinder into the soul-fire (which Adam had turned into a dark coal)—and it glows. And when the light of Divine Power is then ignited within it, the creature must then go forward as an instrument of the Spirit of God and speak what the Spirit of God says. At that point, the soul is no longer its own property, but the instrument of God.

30. But even within this fiery impulse, the soul’s will must without ceasing sink itself into the Nothing, into the highest humility before God. As soon as it attempts to go—even in the smallest part—into its own searching, the Devil reaches it in the center of the life-formation and sifts it, so that it enters back into selfhood. For the soul must remain in yielded humility <term>Gelassenheit: Often translated as "resignation" or "yieldedness," this is the core Böhmean practice of letting go of the self-will to let God work.</term> like a spring at its source; it must without ceasing draw and drink from God’s little fountain, and never desire to depart from God's ways.

31. For as soon as the soul eats of selfhood from the light of reason <term>Vernunft-Licht: Human intellect or "natural" reason, which Böhme warns can lead to spiritual pride if not illuminated by God.</term>, it walks in its own delusion. Then, whatever it presents as Divine is merely the influence of the external constellation <note>original: "äusseren Constellation"; Böhme refers to the "astral" or worldly spirit that governs human psychology and physical nature when one is not centered in God.</note>, which immediately seizes the soul and makes it drunk. It then runs in error for as long as it takes to surrender itself entirely back into yieldedness and once again becomes a soiled child...

<summary>Böhme explains that spiritual enlightenment requires the total surrender of the ego (selfhood) so that the soul becomes a passive instrument for God's Spirit. He warns that the "light of reason" can lead to delusion if the soul stops "drinking" from the divine source and attempts to act on its own.</summary>

### Chapter 1, Section 3: On True Resignation.

...child recognizes, it must die again to reason <term>Vernunft: Often used by Böhme to describe the limited, earth-bound intellect that tries to understand God without divine grace.</term> anew, and reach God's love again; this is more difficult than the first time, for the devil violently introduces doubt into the process, as he does not like to leave his robber-castle <note>original: "Raub-Schloß"; a metaphor for the ego-bound soul that has stolen for itself what belongs to God.</note>.

32. One sees this quite clearly in the Saints of God throughout history: how many were driven by the Spirit of God, and yet sometimes returned from resignation <term>Gelassenheit: A key term meaning yieldedness, surrender, or the state of having let go of one's own will.</term> back into selfhood <term>Selbheit: The ego or the state of being centered on oneself rather than God.</term>—that is, into their own reason and will. In this state, Satan plunged them into sin and God's wrath, as can be seen in David and Solomon, as well as the patriarchs, prophets, and apostles, who sometimes committed powerful errors when they moved from resignation into selfhood—into their own reason and the desires of that reason.

33. Therefore, it is necessary for the children of God to know what they should do with themselves if they wish to learn the way of God: namely, that they must break and cast away their own thoughts. They should desire to learn nothing unless they feel themselves to be in true resignation, so that God's Spirit may teach, guide, and lead the human spirit, and so that the human "own-will" is entirely broken of its own pleasure and surrendered to God.

34. All speculating into the wonders of God is a very dangerous thing, by which the will-spirit may soon be captured—unless the will-spirit follows after the Spirit of God. If it does, then in resigned humility, it has the power to behold all the wonders of God.

35. I am not saying that a person should research or learn nothing of the natural arts <note>Böhme refers here to sciences, crafts, and secular academic disciplines.</note>; no, for those are useful to him. However, one's own reason should not be the starting point. A person should not govern his life solely by the external light of reason; that light is indeed good, but he should sink himself with it into the deepest humility before God, and place the Spirit and will of God at the forefront of all his research, so that the light of reason sees through God's light. And even if reason recognizes much, it should not claim it as its own property, but give the glory to God, to whom alone belong knowledge and wisdom.

36. For the more reason sinks itself into simple humility before God, and the more unworthy it considers itself before God,

->IX. Way to Christ.<-

...the more it <note>The soul, which in German is a feminine noun (*die Seele*), hence "she" in the original text.</note> dies to its own desire, and the more God's Spirit penetrates it and leads it into the highest knowledge, so that it may behold the great wonders of God. For God's Spirit travels only in surrendered humility; that which does not seek or desire itself, that which desires in itself to be simple before God—that, the Spirit of God seizes and carries out into His wonders. Only those who fear Him and bow before Him please Him.

37. For God did not create us for self-dominion <term>Eigen-Herrschaft: The state of being one's own master or acting independently of divine will; autonomy in a negative sense.</term>, but as instruments of His wonders, through which He wishes to reveal His wonders Himself. The surrendered <term>gelassen: A central term for Böhme meaning yielded, surrendered, or having released the ego.</term> will trusts God and hopes for every good from Him; but the own will <note>The "self-will" or ego-driven will.</note> governs itself, for it has broken itself away from God.

38. Everything that the own will does is sin and against God: For it has departed from the order in which God created it into a state of disobedience, and wishes to be its own master.

39. When the own will dies to selfhood <term>Selbheit: The ego-state or the condition of being centered on oneself rather than God.</term>, then it is free from sin: For it desires nothing but that which God desires from His creature; it desires only to do that for which God created it, and what God wishes to do through it. And although it is and must be the "doing" <note>The person remains the active agent performing the task.</note>, yet it is only as an instrument of that doing, with which God does what He wills.

40. For that is exactly the right faith in a human being: that they die to selfhood, that is, to their own desire, and bring their desire in all their undertakings into God's will. They take no ownership of anything for themselves, but in all their work they consider themselves only as God's servant and minister, and think that everything they do and intend, they do for God.

41. For in such a will, the Spirit of God leads them into true faithfulness and honesty toward their neighbor; for they think: "I do not do my work for myself, but for my God, who has called and ordained me for it as a servant in His vineyard." Such a person always listens for the voice of their Lord, who commands them from within what they should do; the Lord speaks in them and commands the action.

42. But selfhood does what external reason <term>äussere Vernunft: Intellectual or worldly logic that relies on sensory perception rather than spiritual revelation.</term> from...

### Chapter 1, Section 3: On True Yieldedness

...the wishes of the constellations, into which the devil—flying within—introduces himself with his desire. Everything that selfhood <term>Selbheit: the ego-driven state of being centered on oneself rather than God</term> does is outside of God's will; it all happens in fantasy <note>In Böhme’s thought, "fantasy" refers to an illusory, self-created reality separate from God's truth.</note>, so that the wrath of God may take its pleasure in it.

43. No work outside of God's will can reach God's kingdom; it is all merely useless carving <note>Referring to man-made idols or meaningless, decorative labor.</note> in the great toil of humanity. For nothing pleases God except what He Himself does through the human will. For there is only one God in the essence of all essences; and everything that works and acts within that same essence with Him is one spirit with Him.

44. But whatever acts in its selfhood in its own will is outside His holy governance <term>Regiment: divine order, rule, or administration</term>, existing only in itself. It is still within His almighty governance—by which He rules all life—but it is not in the *holy* divine governance. Instead, it is in the governance of nature, by which He rules both evil and good. Nothing is called "divine" that does not move and act within God's will.

45. "Every plant," says Christ, "which my heavenly Father has not planted shall be rooted up and burned in the fire" (Matthew 15:13). All works of man which he performs outside of God's will shall all burn in the final fire of God, and be given over to the wrath of God—as the abyss of darkness—for eternal "delight" <note>A dark irony; the "pleasure" of the wrathful abyss is the consumption and destruction of these selfish works.</note>. For Christ says: "He who is not with me is against me; and he who does not gather with me scatters." That is: whoever does not act and work in a yielded <term>gelassen: surrendered, resigned, or released from ego</term> will, in trust upon Him, only wastes and scatters; it is not pleasing to Him. Nothing pleases God except what He Himself wills with His Spirit and does through His instrument <term>Werckzeug: a tool or vessel; Böhme sees humans as the tools through which God expresses His wonders.</term>.

46. Therefore, everything is but "fable and Babel" <note>A play on words: "Babel" represents the confusion of human-made systems and religions, while "fable" suggests they are mere fictions compared to divine truth.</note> that happens through the conclusions of human selfhood without divine knowledge and will. It is only a work of the stars <note>Referring to the "astral" influences or natural fate that governs the physical man.</note> and the outer world, and is not recognized by God as His work; rather, it is a mirror of the wrestling wheel of nature, where good and evil wrestle with one another. What the good builds, the evil breaks; and what the evil builds, the good breaks. And this is the great misery of vain toil, all of which belongs to the judgment of God, to the final separation of the strife.

<meta>catchword: 47. Therefore-</meta>

<summary>Böhme explains that any human action performed from the "self-will" is a product of "fantasy" and astrological influence rather than divine grace. He distinguishes between God's general rule over nature (ruling both good and evil) and His holy governance, which only accepts works done in total surrender to Him.</summary>

IX. Path to Christ.

47. Therefore, whoever works and builds much in such toil and labor, works only toward the judgment of God. For there is nothing perfect or permanent there; everything must go into <term>Putrefaction: an alchemical term for decomposition or decay, which Böhme uses to describe the necessary breaking down of the old self so that a new spiritual life can begin</term> and be separated. For whatever is worked within the wrath of God is taken up by that same wrath and is kept in the <term>Mysterio: Latin for 'mystery', referring here to the spiritual treasury or hidden dimension of human deeds</term> of its own desire until the Day of Judgment, when evil and good shall be separated.

48. But if man now turns around and goes out from <term>Selbheit: selfhood or the ego-driven state of being centered on oneself</term> and enters into God’s will, then the good that he has worked even while in selfhood shall be released from the evil he has worked. For Isaiah says: *Though your sins be as blood-red; if you turn and repent, they shall be made white as wool, like snow.* (Isaiah 1:18). For the evil is swallowed up into death by the wrath of God, and the good goes forth like a plant from the wild earth.

## Chapter 2.
### Summaries.

1. The yielded <note>original: *gelassene*—referring to the state of "Gelassenheit" or spiritual surrender/resignation to God</note> will creates a perfect work and 2. breaks the essence of selfhood. 3. In the darkness, the devil is prince, yet he does not rule in the outward world, 12. but is instead captured by the good; 13. although he is busy in the <term>Turba Magna: Latin for the 'Great Turmoil'; Böhme’s term for the state of chaos, wrath, or disruption within nature</term>. 14. The creature awakens good and evil with its desire; 15. if it goes out from its "mother" <note>Referring to the source or nature from which a thing originates</note>, it enters into reluctance and opposition, 16. but finds only unrest in its own will, 17. just as there is rest in yieldedness. 18. All external "shining" toward God is useless. 33. There is only One way to God. 34. Hypocrisy helps nothing here.

# Chapters 2 & 3. On True Resignation.

<margin>catchword: out,</margin>

34. The soulish <note>original: *seelische*—referring to the natural human soul's independent drive</note> will must die. 35. Outward forgiveness is hypocrisy, 36. we must die to sin. 37. Whoever is now weary of all sin: he can take comfort in Christ’s suffering. 38. 1. Whoever intends to perform anything perfect and good, in which he intends to rejoice eternally and to enjoy, let him go out from <term>Selbheit: selfhood; the ego-driven state of being centered on one’s own desires</term>, as if from his own desire, and enter into <term>Gelassenheit: resignation or yieldedness; the act of surrendering one's will to God</term> in God's will, and work with God.

2. Although the earthly desire of selfhood still clings to him in flesh and blood, so long as the soul-will does not embrace it, selfhood can produce no "work." For the resigned <note>or surrendered</note> will breaks the essence of selfhood again and again, so that the wrath of God cannot reach it. And if it does reach it—which is not entirely impossible and may happen—the resigned will nevertheless carries its power upward within it; thus it stands as a figure before God, as a work of victory in the <term>Wunder: wonder or miracle</term>, and can inherit the divine childhood.

3. Therefore, speaking and doing are not good when reason is inflamed in the desire of selfhood; such desire works instead in God’s wrath, from which man will suffer harm, for his work will be led into God’s wrath and kept until the great Day of Judgment of God.

4. All false desire, whereby a man intends to draw the abundance of the world from his neighbor through cunning—to his neighbor's ruin—is all taken up by God's wrath and belongs to the judgment. There, everything shall be made manifest, and every power and essence, in both good and evil, shall stand before one's eyes in the <term>Mysterio: Latin for "mystery"; the hidden spiritual dimension where all deeds are recorded</term> of the Revelation. Every misdeed done by design belongs to the judgment of God.

5. But he who turns back, he goes out from it again,

...out, but the work belongs to the fire <note>referring to the biblical "testing by fire" where only what is done in God's will survives</note>; everything shall and must become manifest at the end. For God has introduced his working power into a being for this very reason: so that God’s love and wrath might manifest themselves, and that each might be at play, for the glory of God and his wondrous deeds.

6. And it is for every creature to know this: that it should remain in that state in which God created it, or else it runs into the opposition and enmity of God’s will and leads itself into torment. For no creature that was created into the darkness feels pain from the darkness; just as a poisonous worm feels no pain from its poison, for the poison is its life. But if it were to lose its poison, and if something good were introduced into it and became manifest in its <term>Essence: *Essenz*; the fundamental spiritual substance or inner nature of a thing</term>, that would be its pain and its death. In the same way, evil is the pain and death of the good.

7. Man is created into Paradise, in God’s love; and if he leads himself into wrath—as if into a poisonous torment and death—then that contrary life becomes a pain to him.

8. If the devil had been created out of the fierce <term>Matrix: the "womb" or originating source-principle of nature</term> into hell, and had not possessed a divine <term>Ens: *being*; a philosophical term for actual existence or spiritual substance</term>, then he would feel no pain in hell. But because he was created into heaven, yet stirred up the torment of darkness within himself and introduced himself entirely into the dark world, the light is now a pain to him. It is an eternal despair of God's grace and a constant enmity, because he cannot endure the light within himself and has spat it out. Thus, he is angry with his mother who bore him, and is also angry with his father from whose <term>Essence: *Essenz*; fundamental nature</term> and being he originated—that is, the eternal nature, which holds him captive as an apostate out of his <term>Place: original: *Loco*; his rightful spiritual station or position</term>. # IX. The Way to Christ

[de]sire stands in the <term>Center: *Centro*; the core or generative source of a being's life-force</term> of eternal, unbeginning nature; in whatever it is ignited—be it evil or good—the desire brings its effect to completion.

15. Now God has created every thing into that place where it ought to be: the angels into heaven, and man into Paradise. If the desire of the creature moves out from its own mother <note>The "mother" here refers to the source or the natural state from which a being originates.</note>, it enters into opposition and enmity, and therein it is tormented by that opposition. Thus, a false will arises within a good one. Because of this, the good will enters back into its "Nothingness"—that is, to the end of nature and the creature—and leaves the creature in its own malice. This is seen in Lucifer, and also in Adam; had God’s Will of Love not met him and entered back into humanity out of grace, there would likely still be no good will within man.

16. Therefore, all <term>Speculating: *Spintisiren*; over-intellectualizing or idle pondering without spiritual practice</term> and researching concerning God’s will is a futile thing without a conversion of the <term>Mind: *Gemüthe*; the deep inner disposition or soul-center</term>. When the mind stands imprisoned in its own desire for this earthly life, it cannot grasp God’s will; it only runs within <term>Selfhood: *Selbheit*; the state of being focused on one's own ego and selfish desires</term>, from one path to another, and yet finds no rest. For one's own desire always introduces unrest.

17. But when the mind sinks itself entirely into God’s mercy and desires to die to its selfhood, seeking God’s will as its guide and understanding—recognizing and holding itself as a "nothing" that wills nothing except what God wills—then, when the desire of wrath comes through the earthly flesh with the devil’s imagination and strikes against the soul’s will, the <term>Yielded: *gelassene*; surrendered, resigned, or at peace</term> desire cries out to God:
> "Abba, dear Father, deliver me from evil!" <note>original: "Abba lieber Vater". Abba is an Aramaic word for "Father," used as a term of endearment or intimacy.</note>
And then—even if it happens that the earthly will becomes too strong in the wrath of God through the devil’s addiction—it works only within itself, as St. Paul also says:
> Now if I do that which I would not, it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me.
Romans 7:20. Likewise:
> So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin.
Romans 7:25.

18. Paul does not mean that the mind should consent to the will of the flesh; rather, sin in the flesh is so strong, as is the awakened wrath of God in selfhood, that...

21. He has given that power the strength to crush the head of sin in the flesh—the serpent's will and desire. That is to say: the resigned will in Christ treads upon the head of the sinful serpent-will's desire and kills the committed sin again. This given power becomes a death to death, and a power of life unto life.

22. Therefore, no one has an excuse, as if he "could not" will it. Indeed, while he is stuck in Selfhood and in his own desires, serving only the law of sin in the flesh, he cannot; for he is held captive and is a servant of sin. But when he turns the center of the mind around, and turns it toward God’s obedience and will, then he is able.

<page-num>106</page-num>
<header>IX. The Way to Christ.</header>
<meta>catchword: earthly,</meta>

[The Spirit] draws you toward it, yet you yourself do not know it. Oh, how fine it would seem to Adam <note>Böhme uses "Adam" to represent the fallen, selfish nature of humanity</note> if he could be taken into heaven with this [self-]will, and place the evil child, full of falsehood, upon God’s throne. Lucifer also wanted it to be so, but he was spewed out.

43. The dying of the evil will is painful; no one wants to face it. We would all gladly be children [of God] if we could be taken in with this "fur-coat" <note>original: *Pelze*; a metaphor for the coarse, animal-like nature of the fallen human body and its desires</note>, but that simply cannot be. This world passes away, and so the outward life must also die. What use would sonship be to me then, if it were kept in a mortal body?

44. Whoever wishes to inherit sonship must also put on a **new man**, who is capable of inheriting that sonship and who is like the Godhead. God wants no sinner in heaven, but only purely newborn children who have "put on" the heaven.

45. Therefore, it is not such an easy thing to become or be children of God as people describe to us. To be sure, it is easy for the one who has already put on sonship—whose light shines and who finds joy in it. But to turn the mind around and break the selfhood <term>selfhood: *Selbheit*; the egoistic state of being centered on one's own desires rather than God's will</term> requires a rigorous, unyielding earnestness. It requires such a resolution that, even if body and soul should break apart because of it, the will would nonetheless remain steadfast and refuse to return into selfhood.

46. There must be a struggle until the dark, hard, locked center <term>center: *Centrum*; the innermost core of the soul where spiritual transformation begins</term> bursts open, and the spark in the center catches fire. From that spark, the noble lily-branch <note>a recurring symbol in Böhme’s work representing the growth of the new, pure spiritual life</note> immediately grows green (like a divine mustard seed, as Christ says). There must be earnest prayer with great humility; for a time, one must even be a fool in the eyes of one's own reason, seeing oneself as foolish, until Christ takes a form in this new incarnation <term>incarnation: *Menschwerdung*; here referring to the "in-man-ing" or birth of Christ within the individual believer</term>.

47. And then, when Christ is born, Herod immediately comes and wants to kill the child. He seeks to do this outwardly through persecution and inwardly through temptation, to see if this lily-branch will be strong enough to break the devil's kingdom, which is manifest in the flesh.

48. This Crusher of the Serpent <note>original: *Schlangen-Treter*; a title for Christ referring to the prophecy in Genesis 3:15</note> is led into the wilderness after He has first been baptized with the Holy Spirit. He is tempted to see if He will remain in yieldedness <term>yieldedness: *Gelassenheit*; the spiritual practice of surrendering one's will entirely to God</term> within God's will. He must stand so firm that, in the event of a fall, all earthly [things]...

<summary>Böhme explains that becoming a child of God requires the painful death of the "selfhood" and a spiritual struggle to allow Christ to be born within the soul. This internal "new man" must then survive the temptations of the world and the "Herod" of the ego.</summary>
<keywords>selfhood, rebirth, Lily-branch, inner Christ, yieldedness, Gelassenheit, spiritual struggle, temptation</keywords>

<page-num>107</page-num>
### Chapter 2. 3. On True Resignation.
<meta>catchword: 52. The</meta>

[...the soul] abandons the earthly, indeed even the outer life, for the sake of divine sonship.

49. No worldly honor or wealth must be preferred over this sonship; instead, one must willingly forsake it all, not regarding it as one's own, but viewing oneself only as a servant of these things who obeys his Master through them. He must abandon all ownership of this world—not that he should not possess it, or be forbidden from possessing it, but his heart must leave it. He must not let his will enter into his possessions or regard them as his own; otherwise, he has no power to serve the needy with them.

50. Selfhood <term>selfhood: *Selbheit*; the egoistic state of being centered on one’s own desires and "I-ness" rather than God's will</term> serves only the temporal being, but resignation <term>resignation: *Gelassenheit*; a state of yieldedness, surrender, or "letting go" of the self-will to God</term> rules over everything beneath it. Selfhood must do what the devil wants in the lusts of the flesh and a proud life; but resignation treads upon that with the feet of the mind. Selfhood despises what is simple <note>original: *alber*; in Böhme’s time, this meant "simple" or "innocent," though it evolved into the modern German word for "silly"</note>, but resignation lays itself down in the dust with the simple. It says: "I want to be simple and understand nothing, so that my intellect does not exalt itself and sin. I will lie at the feet of my God in His courtyards, so that I may serve my Master however He wishes. I want to know nothing, so that my Master's commandments may guide and lead me, and I only do what God does through me and desires. I will sleep within my selfhood until the Lord wakes me with His Spirit; and if He does not wish it, I will rest eternally in Him in silence and await His command."

51. Dear brothers, people boast of faith nowadays, but where is faith? Today's faith is merely a history <note>original: *Historia*; Böhme distinguishes between "historical faith" (intellectual belief in facts) and "living faith" (a direct experience of God)</note>. Where is the child who believes that Jesus is born? If he existed and truly believed that Jesus was born, he would surely approach the little child Jesus, receive Him, and care for Him. Alas, it is only a historical faith and pure book-knowledge—and much more a tickling of the conscience: [the belief] that the Jews killed Him; that He departed from this world; that He is not King on earth within the animalistic <term>animalistic man: *animalischen Menschen*; the carnal, unrefined nature of man that is driven by biological instincts rather than the Holy Spirit</term> man; that man may do whatever he wants; and that he does not need to die to sin and evil lusts. Selfhood, that wicked child, rejoices in this, so that it may live in luxury and fatten up the devil.

<summary>Böhme explains that true spiritual life requires "resignation" (Gelassenheit)—detaching the heart from worldly ownership and intellectual pride—to become a vessel for God's will. He critiques contemporary religion as a mere "historical faith" that avoids the necessary death of the selfish, carnal nature.</summary>
<keywords>resignation, selfhood, sonship, historical faith, animalistic man, poverty of spirit, Jacob Böhme, spiritual rebirth</keywords>

<page-num>108</page-num>
<header>IX. The Way to Christ.</header>
<meta>catchword: The</meta>

52. The truth is proven: that true faith has never been sicker or weaker since the time of Christ than it is right now—even while the world cries out loudly: "We have found the right faith!" They bicker over a "child" <note>Boehme uses the "child" as a metaphor for the new spiritual life or the state of the Church; here he suggests the "child" of their era is actually filled with wickedness</note> who has never been more wicked since mankind first walked the earth.

53. If you are Zion <note>Zion: a biblical term for the dwelling place of God, used here by Boehme to represent the true, renewed community of believers</note>, the newborn and rediscovered child, then demonstrate your power and virtue. Bring forth the Little Child JESUS from within yourself so that everyone can see you are His wet-nurse. If you cannot, then the children of Christ will say: you have only found the "child of histories" <note>original: *Kind der Historien*; Boehme uses this to describe a faith based only on book-learning, literal history, and intellectual dogma rather than a living, internal experience of God</note>—the mere cradle of the child.

54. Where do you keep the Little Child JESUS, you apostate, with your "histories" and your false, superficial faith? How will the Little Child JESUS visit you within the Father's property—within your own *Turba* <term>Turba: a Latin term meaning "turmoil" or "disturbance"; in Boehme’s theology, it refers to the chaotic, wrathful energy of nature that breaks out when a soul or a society turns away from God's light</term>, which you have fattened so well? He calls to you in love, but you refuse to hear, for your ears are firmly closed by greed and lust. Therefore, the sound of trumpets and a harsh thunderclap shall shatter your *Turba* and wake you, to see if you might yet seek and find the Little Child JESUS.

55. Dear brothers, it is a time of searching, finding, and earnestness. Whomever it strikes, it strikes. Whoever remains awake shall hear and see it. But whoever sleeps in sin, in the "fat days" of his belly, says: "All is peace and quiet; we hear no sound from the Lord." But the Lord’s voice has resounded to the ends of the earth; a smoke arises, and in the midst of the smoke, a great brightness of radiance—Amen! Hallelujah, Amen!

->Rejoice in the Lord in Zion, for all the mountains and hills are full of His glory: He shoots up like a growing plant; who shall prevent it?<-

### Author's Preface.

Although I have sufficiently explained this in my other very deep writings and presented it from its fundamental ground, yet everyone does not have such books in hand, nor is it within everyone’s capacity to understand them; therefore, for the service of the simple children of Christ, and at the request of good friends, I have written a short summary of the new rebirth, to see if anyone might wish to learn to know themselves through it.

2. But whoever desires to search into the deep ground from which this flows, and has the gift of understanding, let him read the book *Of the Threefold Life of Man*; also the three books *Of the Incarnation and Birth of Jesus Christ*; likewise the book *Of the Six Points*; *Of the Great Mystery* <note>original Latin: "Mysterio Magno"</note>; *Of the Three Worlds*, how they stand within one another as one, but make three principles <note>original Latin: "Principia," here meaning foundational sources or beginnings</note>—that is, three births or beginnings, etc.—also the book *Of the Three Principles* <note>original Latin: "de Tribus Principiis"</note>. There he will find whatever he may ask after, as high as a human mind can soar, as well as in the *Forty Questions of the Soul*.

3. This I have now written for those hearts hungry and thirsty for Christ’s little fountain, as my fellow members in the spirit of Christ. To the mockers, however, I have written nothing; for they have their book within themselves, with which they drive the children of Christ under the cross, and they must—against their own will—be servants to the children of Christ, even if they do not understand this.

# The Fourth Little Book.
# ON REGENERATION, <note>original Latin: "DE REGENERATIONE"</note>
->or<-
# Of the New Rebirth.

## Author’s Preface.

Although I have sufficiently explained this in my other very deep writings and presented it from its fundamental ground, not everyone possesses those works, nor is it within everyone’s capacity to understand them. Therefore, for the service of the simple children of Christ, and at the request of good friends, I have written a short summary <note>original: "Summam"</note> of the new rebirth, so that someone might perhaps learn to recognize themselves through it.

2. But whoever desires to search the deep ground from which this flows, and has the gift of understanding, let them read the book *On the Threefold Life of Man*; also the three books *On the Incarnation and Birth of Jesus Christ*; likewise the *Book of Six Points*; on the *Mysterium Magnum* <note>original: "Great Mystery," Böhme's massive commentary on Genesis</note>; on the *Three Worlds*, how they stand within one another as one, yet make three Principles <term>Principles: translated from "Principia," Böhme's term for the three fundamental spiritual realities: the dark fire-world, the light-world, and the external physical world</term>, that is, three births or beginnings, etc. Also the book *On the Three Principles* <note>original Latin: "De Tribus Principiis"</note>: there they shall find whatever they might ask, as high as a human mind can soar, as well as in the *Forty Questions on the Soul*.

3. Now, I have written this for the hungry and thirsty hearts seeking Christ's fountain, as my fellow members in the Spirit of Christ. But to the mockers I have written nothing: for they have their own book within themselves, with which they drive the children of Christ under the cross; and they must be the servants of Christ's children against their own will, even if they do not understand this.

## ON REGENERATION, <note>original: "DE REGENERATIONE"</note>
### or
# Concerning the New Rebirth.

### Author's Preface.
Although I have sufficiently explained this in my other very deep writings and presented it from its foundational source, not everyone has such books in hand, nor is it within everyone’s capacity to understand them. Therefore, for the service of the simple-hearted children of Christ, and at the request of good friends, I have written a short summary <note>Böhme uses "Summam" to mean a condensed overview of his complex theology.</note> concerning the new rebirth, so that one might learn to recognize oneself through it.

### Chapter 1, Section 4: Of the New Rebirth.

4. Yet, since it remains true that a true Christian is born of Christ, and that the new rebirth <note>original: "Wiedergeburt"</note> is a temple of the Holy Spirit who dwells within us—and that only the new man born of Christ partakes of the flesh and blood of Christ—then being a Christian is no small or simple matter. Christianity does not consist merely in "history" <note>the author uses "history" here to mean mere intellectual knowledge or facts about the past</note>, where we only know the facts and claim that knowledge for ourselves, saying: "Christ died for us, he has broken the power of death within us and turned it into life; He has paid the debt for us, we need only take comfort in this and firmly believe it has happened."

5. For we find within ourselves that sin is alive, desiring, and active in the flesh; it is at work. Therefore, the new rebirth out of Christ must be something else, which does not cooperate with the sinful flesh and does not desire sin.

6. For Saint Paul says: "There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus" (Romans 8:1). And further: "If we, who are Christians, were still found to be sinners, would Christ be a servant of sin? God forbid!" (Galatians 2:17), since we have died to sin (in Christ). Furthermore, a man of sin is not a temple of the Holy Spirit; yet there is no man who does not sin. For the Scripture says: "God has consigned all to sin" (Romans 11:32). Likewise: "In your sight, no living person is righteous, if you should mark iniquities" (Psalm 143:2). "The righteous falls seven times a day" (Proverbs 24:16); yet this must not be understood to mean that the "righteous" part falls and sins, but rather the mortal (and sinful) part of the person.

7. For a Christian’s righteousness is in Christ, and that part cannot sin. For Saint Paul says: "Our way of life <note>original: "Wandel"; referring to spiritual conduct or citizenship</note> is in heaven, from whence we also look for the Savior Jesus Christ" (Philippians 3:20). If our way of life is in heaven, then heaven must be within us. Christ dwells in heaven; since we are his temple, then that same heaven must be within us.

8. However, because sin still assails us from within, through which the devil has an entrance to us and into us, then hell must also be within us, for the devil dwells in hell. Wherever he is, he is in hell and cannot leave it. And even if he were to take hold of <note>original: "befasse"; this is the catchword for the following page</note> a person,

9. Just as the flesh must die, so also must the life and the will of sin die. One must become like a child that knows nothing and only groans for the mother who gave it birth. In this same way, the entire will of a Christian must enter back into the Mother—that is, into the Spirit of Christ—and in **selfhood** <note>original: "Selbheit"; this refers to the ego or the self-centered will that acts independently of God</note>, in self-willing and one's own power, become a child. There, the will and desire are directed only toward the Mother; and out of the Spirit of Christ, a new will and obedience must rise from death in righteousness, a will that no longer desires sin.

10. For the will that allows vanity into itself and desires it is not reborn. And if there nonetheless remains a will in the reborn person which longs for vanity and sins, then we must rightly examine the image of man to see how the new rebirth happens. For it does not happen in the mortal flesh, and yet it truly happens within us—in flesh and blood, in water and spirit—just as the Scripture says.

11. Thus we must rightly consider what kind of man is within us who is a member of Christ and a **temple of God**, who dwells in heaven; and then also, what kind of man that is who dwells only in the outer world, and what kind of man that is whom the devil rules and drives. For the devil cannot rule or drive the temple of Christ, and he cares nothing for the mortal flesh; and yet, these are not three separate men inside one another, but only a single man.

...outer world, with the stars and four elements, in which man and all creatures live: This is not and is not called God; God dwells surely within it, but the essence of the outer world does not contain Him. We also have an example of this in the four elements, which in their original state <note>original: "Urstand"; refers to the primordial or fundamental condition of a thing before it is differentiated</note> are only one element, which is neither hot nor cold, neither dry nor wet; yet with movement, it divides itself into four properties, namely into fire, air, water, and earth.

14. Who would believe that fire gives birth to water? And that the origin of fire could be in water, if we did not see this with our own eyes in the lightning <note>original: "Wetter-Leuchten"; literally "weather-shining," referring to heat lightning or the flash of a storm</note>; it is also to be found in living beings, that the essential fire dwells in the body <term>original: "Corpore"; the physical or material vessel of a living being</term>, in the blood, and that the blood is its mother, and the fire is the blood's father.

15. Just as God dwells in the world and fills all things, and yet possesses nothing; and as fire dwells in the water and does not possess it; and as the light dwells in the darkness, and yet does not possess the darkness; the day in the night, and the night in the day; time in eternity, and eternity in time: So also is man created. According to his outer humanity, he is time and exists in time; and time is the outer world, which is also the outer man. But the inner man is eternity, and the spiritual time and world; which also stands in light and darkness, as in God's love (according to the eternal light) and in God's wrath (according to the eternal darkness). This is manifest within him, and his spirit dwells therein, either in the darkness or in the light. Both are in him, the light and the darkness; each dwells in itself, and neither possesses the other.

16. But if one enters into the other and seeks to possess the other, then the other loses its right and power. The suffering part loses its power; for when the light becomes manifest in the darkness, the darkness loses its dark nature and is not recognized. Likewise, conversely, if the darkness rises up in the light and gains power, the light is extinguished along with its power.

eternal darkness in the soul is Hell, an anguish-torment <note>original: "Angst-Qual"; a central term for Böhme, suggesting both a "source" (Quelle) and "torment" (Qual)</note> which is called God’s wrath; and the eternal light in the soul is the Kingdom of Heaven, where the fiery, dark anguish is transformed into joy.

19. Thus we must also consider man: he stands and lives in three worlds. The first is the eternal dark world, the center <note>original: "Centrum"; the focal point or core from which nature unfolds</note> of eternal nature, which gives birth to the fire as the anguish-torment. The second is the eternal light-world, which gives birth to eternal joy and is the divine dwelling place where the Spirit of God dwells, in which the Spirit of Christ takes on human essence and drives out the darkness, so that the darkness must become a cause of joy within the Spirit of Christ and within the light. The third world is the outer visible world, in the four elements and the visible stars <note>original: "Gestirne"; referring to the astrological and spiritual influences of the celestial bodies</note>: although each element contains a star within itself according to its own property, from which desire and quality arise, much like a mind <note>original: "Gemüthe"; the seat of emotions and will</note>.

20. The fire of the light has a good taste, but the taste in the essence of darkness is entirely adverse and hostile; for the forms leading to the fire all stand in the greatest anguish.

8. The third quality of God’s breath was the external air, with the aerial stars: in which the life and constellations of the external being and body resided; this He breathed into his nostrils. And just as time and eternity hang together, and time is born out of eternity, so too did the inner breath of God hang upon the outer; and this threefold soul was breathed into man all at once. Every essence of the <term>body <note>original: "Corporis"; Latin for "of the body"</note></term> received the spirit according to its own quality: Thus, the outer flesh received the outer air with its stars for a rational and growing life, for the revelation of God's wonders; and the body of light, or the heavenly being, received the breath of light as the Divine power: which breath is called the Holy Spirit.

As Adam and Eve fell into this misery, the wrath of nature awoke in every property, and in its desire, it impressed <term>impressed: the spiritual process of shaping or "stamping" a desire into a physical or psychological form</term> the vanity of earthliness and the wrath of God into itself. Then the flesh became coarse and thick, like that of any other animal, and the noble soul was thereby captured in that essence: And the soul saw that it had become an animal in its body, and saw the animal members for reproduction, and the stinking bag of maggots <note>original: "Madensack"; a blunt 17th-century term Böhme uses to describe the digestive system and the corruptible mortal body</note>, into which the desire of the flesh gathered vanity (or disgust). power. And it now depends solely on this: that the soul lead its will out of the vanity of the (corrupted) flesh, and lead it through this open gate into the Spirit of Christ.

Here, a **Christian** should consider why he calls himself a **Christian**, and well observe whether he truly is one. For me to learn to know and understand that I am a sinner, and that **Christ** has killed my sin on the **Cross** and shed His blood for me, does not yet make a **Christian** out of me; the inheritance belongs only to the children. A maid in the house knows well what the mistress likes, but that does not make her the heir to the mistress's goods. The **Devil** also knows that there is a **God**, but that does not make him an angel again. But if the maid in the house marries the mistress's son, she may well come to the inheritance of the mistress's goods.

# IX. Way to Christ.

<margin>The godless person receives the Sacraments unto judgment.</margin>
...to the hypocritical man his hypocritical absolution; so also do the **Sacraments** help him.

9. In the Sacraments it is now manifest, as it is also in the **Office of Teaching** <term>Office of Teaching—the ministry of preaching and providing spiritual instruction</term>. The Covenant is proclaimed; the soul’s partaking occurs, but in the same quality as the soul’s mouth: Just as the outer animal receives bread and wine, which it could also eat at home; and the **fiery soul** <term>fiery soul—the soul in its natural, untransformed state, characterized by restless desire and "fire"</term> now receives the Testament according to its quality, namely, in the **wrath of God**; she receives the essence of the eternal world, but according to the quality of the dark world. As the mouth is, so also is the food that belongs in the mouth. He receives it to his own judgment, in the manner that the godless will see Christ at the Last Judgment as a serious, strict judge; and the holy as a beloved **Immanuel** <note>original: "ImmanuEl"—Hebrew for "God with us."</note>.

10. Against the godless stands God’s wrath open in His Testaments, and against the holy stands the **heavenly corporeality** <term>heavenly corporeality—the spiritual substance or "body" of Christ that nourishes the inner man</term>, and therein the power of Christ, in the holy name of **Jesus**, open. But what does the Holy help the godless, if he cannot enjoy it? What shall take away his sin here? The sin is only stirred up and made manifest.

11. Yet even in the holy, there is no "taking away" of sin through the Sacraments, or forgiveness by them; rather, it is thus: When Christ rises up, then Adam dies in the **serpent-eating** <note>original: "Schlangen-Essens"—referring to the consumption of the forbidden fruit and the "poison" of the serpent in human nature.</note>; when the sun rises, the night is swallowed up in the day, and there is no more night: Such is the forgiveness of sins. The Spirit of Christ eats of His holy essence; the inner man is the vessel of the holy essence: He receives what the Spirit of Christ leads into him, as the temple of God, Christ’s flesh and blood. What does that concern a beast? Or what does it concern the devils, or the soul in God’s wrath? They eat of their heavenly body, in which heaven they dwell, namely in the **abyss**.

12. So also in the **Office of Preaching**: The godless hears what the outer soul of the outer world preaches, and he accepts it as a **history** <note>original: "Historiam"—Böhme uses this Latin term to critique those who know the Bible only as a collection of historical facts rather than a living spiritual reality.</note>: But if there is perhaps stubble or straw in the preaching, he sucks vanity from it, and the soul sucks from it the false poison and murders of the devil; with this she tickles herself, so that she hears how she can judge people. But if the preacher is also a dead man <note>meaning someone who is spiritually dead or unregenerate</note>, and sows poison and disgrace from his **affects** <term>affects—unregulated emotions, worldly passions, or sectarian anger</term>, then the devil teaches, and the devil hears:

True forgiveness is described not as a ritual act, but as the internal rising of Christ which swallows up the sinful nature of Adam.</summary>

# Chapter 6. Of the New Rebirth.

The same teaching is imprisoned in the godless heart and brings forth godless fruits, from which the world has become a **murder-den** <note>original: "Mordgrube"</note> of the devil, so that in both the teacher and the listener there is nothing but vain mocking, blaspheming, scorning, word-wrangling, and biting for personal gain.

13. But in the holy teacher, the **Holy Spirit** teaches; and in the holy listener, the **Spirit of Christ** hears through the soul and the **Divine vessel of the Divine sound** <term>Divine vessel—the spiritual structure of the soul that resonates with God's word like an instrument</term>. The holy person has his church within himself, where he hears and teaches; but **Babel** <term>Babel—Böhme’s term for the confused, hypocritical, and purely institutionalized church</term> has only the stone-heap, where she goes to practice hypocrisy and pretense. She lets herself be seen in beautiful clothes and acts devout and pious; the stone church is her **GOD**, in which she places her trust.

14. The holy person, however, has his church with him and in him at all places; for whether he stands or walks, lies or sits, he is in his church; he is in the true Christian church, in the temple of Christ. The Holy Spirit preaches to him from all **creatures** <term>creatures—all things in the created natural world, which Böhme viewed as a living revelation of God</term>; everything he looks upon, he sees there a preacher of God.

15. Here the mocker will say that I despise the stone church where the congregation gathers. To that I say: No. Rather, I point to the hypocritical **Babylonian harlot** who only commits harlotry with the stone church; she calls herself a Christian but is merely a harlot’s offspring.

16. A true Christian brings his holy church with him into the congregation: his heart is the true church where one should practice divine service. If I were to go to church for a thousand years, and also take the **Sacrament** every week, and even let myself be absolved every day—if I do not have Christ in me, then it is all false, a useless trifle, a mere piece of wood-carving in **Babel**, and there is no forgiveness of sins.

17. The holy person performs holy works out of the holy power of his **mind** <note>original: "Gemüthe"—the deep disposition or inner soul-mind</note>. The work itself is not the reconciliation; rather, it is the building that the true spirit builds in its own essence. It is his dwelling-house, just as the false Christian’s fables are his dwelling-house, where his soul goes in hypocrisy. The outer hearing goes into the outer and works in the outer; and the inner hearing goes into the inner and works in the inner.

18. You may play the hypocrite, howl, cry out, sing, preach, and teach as much as you want—if the **inner teacher** and listener is not open, then it is all nothing but **Babel**.

## Chapter 7.
### Summaries.

A Christian does not wrangle about religion. §. 1. 2. **Babel** <note>Böhme’s term for the confused, divided, and institutionalized church</note> wrangles only about knowledge, 3. wherein the sects are at odds. 4. But a Christian belongs to no sect; 5. he lives in faith, 6. while Babel wrangles over the letters <note>meaning the literal text of scripture without the spirit</note>, 7. which is the work of the devil. 8. Knowledge only reveals to us that we are evil; 12. but true knowledge is revealed by the Holy Spirit. 13. Those people who wrangle about knowledge and God's will are more foolish than birds and beasts; more useless than meadow flowers; worse than thistles and thorns; 14. yes, they are the devil's growth, and drive God's children to prayer. 15.

1. He has enough conflict within himself against his animalistic, evil flesh and blood. He considers himself always a great sinner and stands in awe of God, for his sins stand openly revealed and are in judgment; for the **Turba** <term>Turba—the "source of disturbance" or the wrathful, chaotic principle in nature that seeks to devour the soul</term> locks them within itself, from which the wrath of God scolds him to his face as a guilty person. But the love of Christ breaks through and drives them away, just as the day swallows the night.

2. But for the godless, his sins rest in the sleep of death, and they sprout up from the abyss and bring forth fruits in hell.

3. Christendom in **Babel** wrangles over knowledge—how one should serve, honor, and recognize God, what He is according to His essence and His will; and they teach poorly, claiming that whoever is not in agreement with them in all matters...

### Chapter 7. 4. On the New Rebirth.

...in knowledge and opinion, that he is no Christian, but a heretic.

4. Now I would truly like to see how one could bring all their **sects** together into one that could call itself the Christian Church, since they are all nothing but despisers of one another, where every group slanders the other and cries them out as false.

5. A Christian, however, has no sect; he can dwell in the midst of sects, even appear in their divine service, and yet clings to no sect. He has only a single **knowledge** <term>Wissenschaft—in Böhme's context, this refers to a deep, experiential spiritual awareness or "science" of the soul, rather than mere academic learning</term>, which is Christ in him. He seeks only one way, which is the desire that he would always gladly do and live rightly, and he places all his knowing and willing into the life of Christ. He sighs and wishes constantly that God's will might happen in him, and His kingdom be revealed in him; he kills sin in the flesh daily and hourly: for the **woman’s seed** <note>original: "des Weibes Same"; a reference to the promise in Genesis 3:15</note>, as the inner man in Christ, constantly treads upon the devil’s head in vanity. Genesis 3:15.

6. His faith is a desire for God, which he has wrapped in certain hope; therein he ventures upon the words of the promise; he lives and dies therein, and yet, according to the true man, he never dies. For Christ says also thus: *Whoever believes in me will never die, but has passed through from death to life.* Also: *Streams of living water will flow from him* <note>original: "Ströhme des lebendigen Wassers"; references to John 11:25-26 and John 7:38</note>, as good doctrine and works.

7. Therefore, I say, all is **Babel** <note>Böhme’s term for the confusion, division, and strife found in institutionalized religious systems</note> that bites one another and wrangles over the **letters** <note>original: "Buchstaben"; refers to the literal, superficial reading of scripture without spiritual understanding</note>. The letters all stand in one root, which is the Spirit of God: just as the various flowers all stand in the earth and all grow beside one another; none bites the other over colors, smell, or taste; they let the earth and sun, as well as rain and wind, heat and cold, do with them what they will, but each grows in its own **essence** <term>Essentz—the essential spiritual substance or inner nature of a thing</term> and property. So it is also with the children of God; they have various gifts and knowledge, but all from One Spirit. They rejoice beside one another in the great wonders of God and thank the Most High in His wisdom: why should they long wrangle about that in which they live and are, and of whose being they themselves are?

### IX. The Way to Christ.

8. It is the greatest folly in **Babel** <note>Böhme uses "Babel" to represent the "City of Confusion," referring to the fragmented and quarreling state of organized churches and worldly systems</note> that the devil has made the world quarrelsome regarding religion, so that they fight over self-made opinions and the **letter** <note>referring to literalist interpretations of scripture</note>; yet the Kingdom of God does not stand in any opinion, but in power and in love. Christ also said, and left it as a final word to His disciples: that they should love one another, and by this everyone would know that they were His disciples, just as He had loved them. If people strove as much for love and righteousness as they do for opinions, there would be no strife at all on earth: we would live as children in our Father, and would need no law or **order** <note>referring to formal religious rules or denominations</note>.

9. For God is served with no law, but with obedience alone: Laws are for the sake of the wicked, who do not desire love and righteousness; they are driven and compelled by laws. We all have but one single **Order**, which is that we hold ourselves still before the Lord of all beings, and surrender our will to Him, and let His Spirit work, play, and do in us what He wills; and whatever He works and reveals in us, we offer that back to Him as His fruit.

10. If we did not quarrel over various fruits, gifts, and knowledge, but recognized one another as children of God’s Spirit, what would judge us? For the Kingdom of God does not depend on our knowing and **imagining** <note>original: "Wähnen"—referring to subjective, often false, human assumptions</note>, but in the power.

11. If we did not know half as much and were much more childlike, but only had a brotherly will toward one another, and lived as children of one mother—as the branches on a tree, which all take sap from one root—then we would be much holier.

12. Knowledge is only for this end (that we learn it) because we have lost the **Divine Power** in Adam, and are now inclined toward evil; so that we may learn to recognize how we have evil qualities within us, and that evil-doing does not please God—so that with knowledge, we may learn to do right. But if we have the power of God in us, and desire with all our strength to do right and live right, then knowledge is merely our **play** <note>original: "unser Spiel"—in Böhme's theology, the "Divine Play" refers to the joyful manifestation of God's wisdom through creation</note>, in which we rejoice.

13. For true knowledge is the revelation of God’s Spirit through eternal wisdom: He knows in His children what He wills; He pours His wisdom and wonders through His children.

<summary>Böhme argues that true faith consists of love and surrender to God's power rather than sectarian dogmas or laws, which are only necessary for the wicked. He suggests that spiritual knowledge should be a source of joy and divine revelation rather than a cause for conflict.</summary>

# IX. The Way to Christ.
<meta>catchword: his</meta>

...how we have fallen from **Unity** into **disunity**, malice, and injustice, and how we have awakened these things within ourselves. Secondly, where we were when we existed in Unity, when we were children of God. Thirdly, how we are now in disunity, in conflict and reluctance. Fourthly, where we are traveling to from this fragile life (this state of being). Where we intend to go with the immortal part, and also with the mortal part.

2. In these four points stands our entire religion: to learn how to come out of disunity and vanity, and to enter again into the **One Tree**—from which we all came in Adam—which is **Christ in us**. We have no need to fight about anything, nor do we have any conflict; let everyone simply practice how they may enter again into the love of God and of their brother.

3. Christ’s Testaments <note>original: "Testamenta"—referring to the sacraments and the New Covenant</note> are absolutely nothing other than a brotherly bond, in which God binds Himself to us in Christ, and we to Him. All teaching should aim toward this, as should all willing, living, and doing. Anything that teaches or acts otherwise is **Babel** <note>Böhme uses "Babel" to describe the "City of Confusion," or the institutionalized, warring churches of his day</note> and fables; it is merely an artificial carving of pride, a useless judgment, and a way of leading the world astray—a hypocrisy of the devil, with which he blinds the simple-hearted.

4. Everyone who teaches outside of God’s Spirit and lacks Divine knowledge, yet sets themselves up as a teacher in God’s kingdom and wants to serve God with teaching, is false. They serve only their **belly-idol** <note>original: "Abgott Bauche"—a reference to Philippians 3:19, describing those who prioritize worldly gain and physical appetites over spiritual truth</note> and their own proud, haughty mind, desiring to be honored and called "Holy." They hold an office chosen by the children of men, who merely flatter them and have appointed them for the sake of favor. Christ spoke: *Truly, truly, I say to you, he who does not enter the sheepfold by the door—that is, through Him—but climbs in another way, is a thief and a murderer, and the sheep do not follow him, for they do not know his voice.* <note>John 10:1-5</note>

5. Such a person does not have the voice of the Spirit of God, but only the voice of his own art and his learning; he teaches, but God’s Spirit does not. Yet Christ says: *Every plant which my heavenly Father has not planted shall be rooted out.* <note>Matthew 15:13</note> How then shall he plant heavenly plants, he who is godless, seeing that he has no seed within...

->### Chapter 8: Concerning the New Rebirth<-

...has His power within it? Christ says plainly: "The sheep do not hear his [the false shepherd’s] voice; they do not follow him." <note>John 10:5</note>

6. The written word is only an **instrument** <note>original: "Werckzeug"—meaning a tool or vessel</note> with which the Spirit leads. The word that seeks to teach must be alive within the literal word. The Spirit of God must be in the literal **sound** <note>original: "Halle"—meaning the resonance or echo of the spoken/written word</note>, otherwise no one is a teacher of God, but only a teacher of letters—a knower of **histories** <note>Böhme uses "histories" to refer to intellectual, factual knowledge of the Bible that lacks personal spiritual experience</note> and not of the Spirit of God in Christ. Everything through which one wishes to serve God must happen in faith, which is to say in the Spirit; that makes the work complete and acceptable before God. Whatever a person begins and does in faith, they do in the Spirit of God, who works along with them in the deed. This is pleasing to God, for He has made it Himself, and His power is within it; it is holy.

7. But what is done in **selfhood** <note>original: "Selbheit"—the state of being focused on the ego and one's own desires rather than God's will</note> without faith is only a figure or a mere aid toward a true Christian work.

8. If you serve your brother and do it only out of **hypocrisy** <note>original: "Gleißeney"—literally "glittering," referring to a shiny outward appearance that masks a false interior</note>, and give to him reluctantly, then you are not serving God. For your faith does not proceed from love into the hope of your gift. You may well serve your brother, and he for his part thanks God and also blesses you; but you do not bless him, for you give to him with a grumbling spirit in your gift. This does not enter into God’s Spirit, nor into the hope of faith. Therefore, your gift is only half-given, and you have only half a reward for it.

9. The same is to be understood regarding receiving: if someone gives in faith and divine hope, they bless their gifts in their faith. But the one who receives them ungratefully and grumbles in spirit curses them in the **partaking** <note>original: "Nieſſung"—the act of consuming, using, or enjoying the gift</note>. Thus, what belongs to each person remains theirs; what they sow, they shall also reap.

10. The same applies to the **teaching office** <note>original: "Lehr-Amt"—the professional ministry or position of a preacher</note>: what a person sows, they shall also reap. If one sows good seed from Christ’s Spirit, it takes root in a good heart and bears good fruit. But in the godless, who are not capable of receiving it, the wrath of God is stirred up. If one sows strife, contempt, and misinterpretation, all godless people take that in; it also takes root and bears such fruit that people mock, deride, slander, and misinterpret one another.

# IX. The Way to Christ.

11. From which the great **Babylon** <note>original: "Babel"—for Böhme, this signifies the confusion of the institutional church and the prideful wrangling over doctrine</note> was born and has grown: because out of pride people wrangle over the **history of justification** <note>Böhme uses "history" (Historiam) to refer to purely intellectual or factual knowledge of scripture that lacks internal spiritual experience</note> of the poor sinner before God. This confuses the simple-hearted and makes them crave novelty, so that one brother despises the other for the sake of histories and the exchange of letters, and hands him over to the devil.

12. Such **vessels of vice** <note>original: "Lasterbälge"—a derogatory term for those filled with malice or worldly corruption</note> do not serve God, but rather the great structure of discord. Because a corrupted desire still lies within the earthly flesh of all humans, they awaken this abomination even in the simple children of God. They cause God’s people, along with the children of wickedness, to become blasphemous. They are merely builders of the great Babylon and of the world, and are about as useful as a **fifth wheel on a wagon**, except that they help erect the structure of hell.

13. Therefore, it is highly necessary for the children of God to pray earnestly and recognize this false noise of construction; they must depart from it in their spirits and not help to build it, nor persecute the children of God themselves, lest they be hindered and led astray from the Kingdom of God. As Christ said to the Pharisees: "Woe to you, Pharisees! You travel over land and sea to win a single convert <term>proselyte</term>, and when he has become one, you make him twice as much a child of hell as yourselves." <note>Matthew 23:15</note> This truly happens among the current factions and sects, and with the shouting and **quarrel-teachers**.

14. Therefore, out of the gifts opened to me by God, I wish to faithfully warn all children of God who intend to be members of Christ against such abominable quarreling and **blood-drums** <note>original: "Blut-Paucken"—referring to inflammatory rhetoric or "war-drumming" that incites sectarian hatred</note>; they should withdraw from brotherly strife and strive simply for love and righteousness toward all people.

15. For if one is a good tree, he shall also bear good fruit: even if he must sometimes endure having the **swine** <note>referring to the ungodly or the worldly-minded</note> devour his fruit, he should nevertheless remain a good tree. He should constantly desire to work with God and not let himself be overcome by any evil. Thus he stands in God’s field and bears fruit for God’s table, which he shall enjoy eternally. Amen.

### Summaries.

Self-interest <note>German: "Eigenheit," referring to the selfish ego or self-will.</note> hinders God. § 1-5. How to enter into the supersensual life? 6, 7. How man can rule over the creatures through renunciation? 8-10. How to advise a person so that the Holy Spirit remains with them constantly? 11, 12. How one must leave everything and take up Christ's cross <note>original: "†"</note>? 13. How one shall come into strength? 14. What great treasure resignation <term>Gelassenheit: a central Böhme concept meaning a state of humble yieldedness or letting go of the self-will to allow God to act.</term> brings? 15. Wherein the body becomes an enemy to evil, 16. and all suffering finally becomes joy. 17. Thereby one becomes conformed to Christ. 18. But from where does one have bread <note>meaning daily sustenance or spiritual nourishment</note> if the world's disfavor falls upon them? 19. God drives such a person to prayer through such trials. ibid. Even if one loses their good friends, 20. they receive all godly souls as brothers and members. 21. What is difficult at first becomes very easy afterward, 22. for one is clothed with heavenly wisdom, 23. so that one can love and hate oneself as is proper, 24. Love and sorrow stand together. 25. What is love? 26. The virtue of love is the "Nothing"; its power is through everything; it is as high as GOD, 27. indeed, greater than God. ibid. Whoever finds it, finds Nothing, and yet finds everything. ibid. It dwells in man where he does not dwell, 28. namely, in the resigned soul. 29. It cannot be grasped. 30. Few find it because they all seek it in "Something" <note>The "Something" (Etwas) refers to created things and the ego, whereas the "Nothing" (Nichts) refers to the divine source beyond all things.</note>; 31. Its office is to burn away the I-hood <note>German: "Ichheit," the state of being centered on the "I".</note>. 32, 33. How to find it most closely? 34. If one wished to walk contrary to everyone, would one be hated by everyone? Answer: one must do right when the world does evil, 35. where the anguish of the flesh works repentance, for the way to the love of the world is foolish. ibid. Where the soul departs when the body dies? 36. It enters with its will into Love or Wrath. 37. How this happens in godly and godless souls? 38. How the Kingdom of God is often hidden in the godly? 39. The godless also feels hell well enough, but does not understand it. ibid. Where do the angels and the devils dwell? 40. How is this to be understood? 41. How far are Heaven and Hell from one another? 42. Heaven is a revelation of the Eternal One, where everything works and wills in silent love: but Hell works in selfhood <note>German: "Selbheit"</note> and false will. ibid. What is an angel and the soul of man? 43. Where does God's love work? ibid. What is the body? 44. What will be after this world? 45. What is the Judgment? ibid.

1. The Disciple spoke to the Master: How may I come to the **supersensual life** <note>Life that is "above the senses" or beyond physical perception.</note>, that I may see God and hear Him speak? The Master spoke: When you can swing yourself for one moment into that place where no creature dwells, then you hear what God speaks.

2. The Disciple spoke: Is that near or far? The Master spoke: It is in you; and if you can be silent for one hour from all your willing and thinking, then you will hear the unspeakable words of God.

3. The Disciple spoke: How can I hear, if I stand still from thinking and willing? The Master spoke: When you stand still from the thinking and willing of your <term>Selfhood: "Selbheit" in German; the state of being driven by the selfish ego or independent "I".</term>, then the eternal hearing, seeing, and speaking will be revealed in you, and God hears and sees through you. Your own hearing, willing, and seeing prevents you, so that you neither see nor hear God.

4. The Disciple spoke: With what shall I hear and see God, since He is above nature and creature? The Master spoke: When you are silent, then you are that which God was before nature and creature, out of which He created your nature and creature: So you hear and see it with that, with which God saw and heard in you, before your own willing, seeing, and hearing began.

5. The Disciple spoke: What holds me back then, that I may not reach it? The Master spoke: Your own willing, hearing, and seeing, and that you strive against that from which you have come: With your own willing, you break yourself off from God's will, and with your own seeing, you see only into your own willing; And your willing stops your hearing with the self-centeredness of earthly, natural

### 5. Of the Supersensual Life.

6. The Disciple spoke: Since I stand in nature, how may I come through nature into the supersensual ground without the breaking of nature? The Master spoke: Three things are required for that. The first is that you surrender your will to God, and sink yourself to the very ground of His mercy. The second is that you hate your own will and do not do that which your will drives you to do. The third is that you subject yourself in patience to the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that you may endure the temptation of nature and creature. And if you do this, God will speak into you <note>Original German: "einsprechen," meaning to breathe into or divinely inspire the soul.</note> and lead your <term>resigned: "Gelassen," a central concept in German mysticism meaning a state of yieldedness or letting go of the self-ego.</term> will into Himself, into the supernatural ground; then you will hear what the Lord speaks in you.

7. The Disciple spoke: So I would have to leave the world and my life if I did that? The Master spoke: If you leave the world, you come into that out of which the world was made. And if you lose your life and come into the powerlessness <note>A state of mystical "poverty" where the individual's ego-driven strength is emptied.</note> of your own ability, then your life stands in that for whose sake you left it—namely in God, from whom it came into the body.

The Disciple spoke: God created man for the natural life, that he should rule over all creatures on earth and be a lord over all life in this world; therefore, he must surely possess it as his own property. The Master spoke: If it is so that you rule over the creatures only externally, then you are in your will and your dominion of an **animal nature**, and you stand only in a figurative, perishable dominion. You also lead your desire into animal essences, by which you become infected and captured, and you also take on an animal nature. But if you have left the figurative nature, you stand in the **Beyond-form** <note>Original: "Uber-Bildlichkeit." This refers to a state of being above all mental images, symbols, or physical forms, returning to the pure essence of God.</note> and rule in the Ground over all creatures from which they were created; and nothing on earth may harm you, for you are equal with all things, and nothing is unequal to you.

### IX. Way to Christ.

...the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, where He spoke: <note>original: "Es sey dann daß ihr umkehret, und werdet als die Kinder, sonst sollet ihr GOttes Reich nicht sehen."</note> Unless you turn and become as little children, you shall not see the Kingdom of God (Matthew 18:3). If it is your intent to be rid of all things, then you must leave all things, and turn your desire away from them. You must not desire them, nor take them upon yourself to possess as a <term>property: "Eigenthum," which in Böhme's thought refers to the ego's claim of ownership over the self and the world.</term> that is "Something." For as soon as you grasp that "Something" into your desire, and let it into yourself to take as your own, then that "Something" is one thing with you, and it works with you in your will. You are then bound to protect it and care for it as if it were your own being. 

But if you take nothing into your desire, then you are free from all things, and you rule over all things all at once. For you have nothing in your receptivity; you are a "Nothing" to all things, and all things are likewise a "Nothing" to you. You are like a child who does not understand what a "thing" is; and even if you do understand it, you understand it without it touching your sensitivity <note>The emotional or physical attachment that pulls the soul away from God.</note>, in the same way that God rules and sees all things, yet no "thing" can grasp Him. 

As for what you said—that I should teach you how you might achieve this—look to the words of Christ, who spoke: <note>original: "Ohne mich könnet ihr nichts thun."</note> Without me you can do nothing (John 15:5). You cannot, by your own power, come to such a rest where no creature touches you, unless you surrender yourself entirely into the life of our Lord Jesus Christ, and hand over your willing and desiring completely to Him, willing nothing without Him. 

Then, you stand with your body in the world among the various qualities of nature, and with your reason <note>In this context, the analytical or worldly mind.</note> you stand under the Cross of our Lord Christ; but with your will, you walk in Heaven. You stand at the "End," the source from which all creatures have come and to which they return. In this state, you may look upon all things outwardly with your reason, and look upon them inwardly with your mind; and with Christ, to whom all power is given in heaven and on earth (Matthew 28:18), you rule in and over all things.

He emphasizes that this state of rest cannot be achieved by human effort alone, but only through total surrender to the life of Jesus.</summary>

### IX. Way to Christ.
