24. The **Disciple** spoke: But how can these two stand together, that a man should love and also hate himself? The **Master** spoke: In that which you love yourself, you do not love yourself as a <term>self-possession: original "Deinheit," meaning "thine-ness" or the quality of belonging to oneself.</term>, but as a given love of **GOD**: you love the **Divine Ground** in you, through which you love **God’s** wisdom and wonders along with your brothers. But in that which you hate yourself, you do so according to the <term>I-ness: original "Ichheit," referring to the selfish ego or the individual will that separates itself from the divine whole.</term>, in which evil clings to you; you do this because you would gladly break the selfhood entirely, so that it might become a purely **Divine Ground** for you. Love hates the selfhood because the selfhood is a mortal thing, and they cannot well dwell together; for love possesses heaven and dwells in itself, but the selfhood possesses the world with its essence and also dwells in itself. Just as heaven rules over the world, and eternity over time, so also does love rule over the natural life.

25. The **Disciple** spoke: Dear Master, tell me then: why must love and sorrow, friend and foe, stand together? Would it not be better if it were nothing but love? The **Master** spoke: If love did not stand in sorrow, it would have nothing to love; but because its essence which it loves—namely the poor soul—stands in sorrow and pain, it has cause to [give] its own be... <note>The text cuts off mid-word "wesen" (being/essence) as it moves to the next page.</note>

<summary>The Master explains the paradox of spiritual life: how the soul must hate its own selfish ego (Ichheit) while loving the Divine Ground within. He teaches that earthly contempt is actually beneficial as it targets the mortal self, and that love requires the presence of sorrow to fulfill its purpose.</summary>

### 5. Of the Supersensual Life.

There is sown a natural, coarse, and elemental body, which in this time is like the outer elements; and in that same coarse body is the subtle power, just as in the earth there is a subtle, good power which compares and unites itself with the sun, and which also in the beginning of time sprang from Divine power, from which the good power of the body was also taken. This good power of the mortal body shall return in a beautiful, transparent, crystalline, material property, in spiritual flesh and blood, and remain or live eternally. Just as then the good power of the earth shall also be, for the earth will also be crystalline, and the Divine light will shine in all being. ### IX. The Way to Christ.

[How is it that in] this time it happens that such conflict exists? The Disciple asked. The Master said: Life exists in conflict so that it may become manifest, sensible, and findable, and so that Wisdom may be discerning <note>Original: *schiedlich*. In Böhme's thought, this refers to the capacity for the unified Divine Wisdom to differentiate into various qualities and forms.</note> and known. And it serves for the eternal joy of overcoming. For among the holy ones in Christ, a great praise shall arise from the fact that Christ has overcome the darkness and all selfhood <term>selfhood: *Eigenheit*. A central term in Böhme's philosophy, referring to the ego-driven nature that separates itself from God's unity to serve its own desires.</term> of nature within them, and that they are delivered from the conflict. They shall rejoice in this eternally when they see how the godless are repaid. 

Thus God allows all things to stand in the free will, so that the eternal dominion—according to love and wrath, according to light and darkness—may be revealed and known, and so that every life may cause and awaken its own judgment within itself. For what is now a conflict and pain to the holy ones in their misery shall be transformed for them into great joy; and what is a pleasure and joy to the godless in this world shall be turned for them into eternal pain and shame. And therefore, the joy of the holy ones must arise out of death, just as the light arises from the candle through the dying and consuming in the fire; so that life may thus be freed from the painfulness <note>Original: *Peinlichkeit*. This refers to the "pangs" or the churning, restless quality of nature before it finds the light of God.</note> of nature and possess another world. 

Just as the light has a completely different property than the fire—giving of itself, while the fire takes and devours itself—so also the holy life of gentleness <note>Original: *Sanftmuth*. Often translated as meekness, it represents the receptive, peaceful state of the soul in God.</note> blossoms out through death, where the self-will dies and God's will of love alone rules and acts in all things.

For in this way, the Eternal has taken on a sensibility and a discernibility, and has led itself out again through death with that sensibility into a great kingdom of joy, so that there may be an eternal play in the infinite unity, and an eternal cause for the kingdom of joy; thus, the painfulness must be a foundation and cause for such movement.

And in this lies the mystery of the hidden wisdom of God.

Whoever asks, receives; whoever seeks, finds; and to him who knocks, it shall be opened. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit, be with us all, Amen.

IX. The Way to Christ.
<meta>catchword: 4. Against</meta>

reason thinks, 38. and because it does not feel the punishment immediately, it thinks there is no longer any seriousness, 39. and looks only at the external. 40. But the wise man hates himself, 41. man should be a man according to God's Spirit. 42.

1. Reason <note>original: *Vernunft*; in Böhme’s thought, this refers to the earthly, logical mind that is limited by sensory experience and cannot perceive spiritual truths on its own.</note> speaks: I hear much said of God, that there is a God who has created all things, also sustains and bears all things; But I have seen none yet or heard from one who has seen God, or who could say: Where God dwells or is, or how He is. For when it beholds the essence of this world, and considers how it goes for the pious as for the evil: And how all things are mortal and fragile; Also how the pious sees no savior who redeems him from the anxiety and adversity of the evil, and thus must go to the pit <note>original: *Gruben*; a common biblical metaphor for the grave or the state of death.</note> with anxieties in misery; So it thinks, all things happen thus by chance <note>original: *ohngefähr*; meaning accidentally or without divine providence.</note>, there is no God who takes care of the suffering, because He lets him who hopes in Him stay stuck in misery, and therein go to the pit; and one has also heard from none who has come back from corruption <note>original: *Verwesung*; referring to the decay of the body after death.</note> and said he had been with God.

2. Answer. Reason is a natural life, whose ground <term>original: *Grund*; a central term in German mysticism referring to the foundational essence or "bottom" of a thing, here meaning the origin of natural existence.</term> stands in a temporal beginning and end, and may not come into the supernatural ground, wherein God is understood: For though it thus beholds itself in this world, and in its contemplation <note>original: *Beschaulichkeit*; the act of looking at or observing the world through the senses.</note> finds no other ground, yet it feels within itself a desire after a higher ground, wherein it may rest:

3. For it understands that it has come from a supernatural ground, and that there must be a God who has brought it into a life and will, and is terrified within itself before its will of wickedness, it is ashamed within itself of its own will, and judges itself in the will of the evil for injustice: Though it does the injustice, nonetheless it accuses itself, and fears a judgment that it does not see; Which indicates that the hidden God, who has brought himself into nature, dwells in it, and punishes it for the evil way, and that this same (hidden God) must not be of the nature of sensibility, because reason does neither see nor grasp him.

<summary>Böhme presents the argument of "Reason," which doubts God's existence due to the presence of suffering and the lack of sensory proof, then counters that the soul's inner conscience and longing for a "higher ground" prove a hidden divine presence.</summary>

### Chapter 1. 6. On Divine Contemplation

->L 4<-

4. On the other hand, the abandoned Reason <note>original: *Vernunft*; the limited, earthly intellect</note>, which feels itself (in its own opinion) to be unjustly tormented in misery, feels a desire within itself to abandon itself even further. It yields itself willingly to suffering, but through its experience of "unjust suffering," it enters into a hope that it will eventually take into itself that which created it, moving beyond the suffering. It desires to rest in that which is not subject to suffering; it seeks rest in that which it is not itself. It desires the death of its **I-ness** <note>original: *Ichheit*; a term in Böhme’s philosophy for the selfish, individualistic ego that separates itself from God</note>, yet it does not desire to be nothing. Rather, it only desires to die to the torment so that it may rest within itself.

5. It yields itself to suffering so that the power of the torment might kill its own suffering. Thus, in its life, through the death of its **self-dying**—inasmuch as it is a painful life—it might enter into the painless and the un-suffering.

6. In this, one rightly understands the **hidden God**: how He reveals Himself in the mind <note>original: *Gemüthe*; the deep-seated disposition or soul-center of a person</note> of man, how He punishes injustice in the conscience, and how He draws the one who suffers unjustly to Himself through that very suffering. One sees how the life of Reason—as the natural life—must, through suffering, be overcome by a desire to turn back into that from which it first came. It must desire to hate itself and die to its natural will so that it may reach the supernatural.

7. Reason speaks: Why has **God** created a painful, suffering life? Could it not exist in a better state without suffering and torment, since He is the **Ground** <term>original: *Grund*; the foundational essence or source of all being</term> and beginning of all things? Why does He tolerate this opposition? Why does He not break the evil, so that only the good exists in all things?

8. Answer: No thing can become manifest to itself without **adversity** <note>original: *Wiederwärtigkeit*; Böhme uses this to mean a "counter-stroke" or resistance. Without a "No," the "Yes" has nothing to stand against and cannot be known.</note>. For if it has nothing that resists it, it always moves outward and never returns into itself. But if it does not return into itself—as into that from which it originally originated—then it knows nothing of its **original state** <note>original: *Urstand*; the primordial condition or source of existence</note>.

<header>### IX. The Way to Christ</header>

God is unknown to the natural life. 10. Thus we can also philosophize about the will of God and say: If the hidden God, who is only one single Being and Will, had not moved Himself out of Himself with His will, and had not moved out of Eternal Science in a <term>tempered balance</term> <note>original: *Temperamento*; the harmonious state where all spiritual qualities are perfectly balanced and unified</note> into a distinctness of the will, and had not led that same distinctness into a graspability for a natural and creaturely life—and if that same distinctness in life were not in conflict—how then would the hidden will of God, which in itself is only One, be revealed to Him? How can there be a knowledge of itself in a single Will?

11. But if there is a distinctness in the One Will, so that the distinctness leads itself into <term>centers</term> <note>original: *Centra*; the individual focal points or "hubs" of separate existence</note> and its own individual will, so that in that which is separated there is a private will, and thus in one single Will, unfathomable and innumerable wills arise, like branches from a tree; then we see and understand that in such distinctness every separate will leads itself into its own form, and that the struggle of the wills is over the form—that one form in its partiality is not like the other, and yet they all stand in One Ground.

12. ### Chapter 1. 6. On Divine Contemplation.

13. Thus Reason speaks: What use is it, or why is it necessary, that evil must exist alongside the good? Answer: Evil or that which is contrary causes the Good—that is, the Will—to press back toward its <term>original state</term> <note>original: *Urstand*; the primal, foundational condition of a being</note>, which is toward God, so that the Good, as a good will, becomes desiring. For a thing that is in itself only good and has no quality of suffering or pain <note>original: *Qual*; Böhme uses this to mean both "quality" and "source of pain/agitation"</note> desires nothing; for it knows nothing better within or before itself for which it could long.

14. So we may also philosophize concerning the single good Will of God and say that He can desire nothing within Himself, for He has nothing within or before Him that could give Him anything. Therefore, He leads Himself out of Himself into a <term>distinctness</term> <note>original: *Schiedlichkeit*; the state of being differentiated or separated into distinct parts</note> and into **centers**, so that a contrariety arises in the outflowing—that is, in that which has flowed out—so that the Good might become perceptible, active, and willing within the Evil. Namely, it wills to separate itself from the Evil and return again into the Single Will of God.

15. But because the outflow of the single, eternal Will of God continually goes out of itself toward its own **revelation**, so also the Good—as the Divine Power—flows out from the Eternal One with such an outflow, entering into the distinctness and into the **centers** of multiplicity.

16. Now, the perpetual outflow of the Will causes the Good within it to move; and through this movement, the Good longs for its original stillness again and becomes desiring to penetrate back into the Eternal One. In such a penetration into itself, the One becomes mobile and full of desire; and in such an operation consists sensitivity, knowledge, and the will.

17. God, insofar as He is called "God," can will nothing but Himself: For He has nothing before or after Him that He could will. If He wills anything, it has flowed out of Him and is a <term>counter-image</term> <note>original: *Gegenwurf*; an object or reflection cast by the subject</note> of Himself, wherein the Eternal Will wills within its own "Something." Now, if that "Something" were only one single thing, the Will would have no way to accomplish anything within it. Therefore, the <term>unfathomable will</term> <note>original: *ungründliche Wille*; the "Ungrund" or the will that has no ground, basis, or cause outside itself</note> divided itself in the beginning and enclosed itself in "being" <note>original: *Wesen*; essence or substance</note>, so that it might act within something, just as one sees an analogy in the human **mind**.

# Chapter I. 6. On Divine Contemplation

...[no] tyrant <note>original: *Herrscher*; likely completing a word from the previous page</note> may set himself up over the inner foundation and destroy the true image of **God**.

37. Earthly **Reason** does not understand this, for she does not know how **God** dwells within her, nor what **God's** will and essence might be. She does not know that **God** dwells through her and is thus near to her, and that her life is but a folly of **Wisdom** through which **Wisdom** reveals herself so that it may be known what **Wisdom** is. Her will has entered from **God** into **selfhood** <term>Selbheit: the state of being trapped in one's own ego and selfish desires, separated from the divine will</term> and boasts of its own power, not seeing how her power has a beginning and an end. She does not see that it is only a **reflection** <note>original: *Spiegel-Werck*; literally "mirror-work," a common Böhme concept where the physical world reflects spiritual realities</note> through which **Wisdom** gazes for a time into the foolishness of the "wise." Finally, through the suffering of the godless, **Wisdom** breaks the folly of those who think themselves wise, as they begin to hate this fragile, foolish life, dying to their **Reason** and surrendering their will to **God**.

38. Earthly **Reason** considers this to be foolishness, especially when she sees that **God** also abandons the earthly folly of the wise and lets the body of such folly—in which that folly was once displayed—go to the grave without help. Thus, she thinks this person has received no salvation from **God**; because he trusted in Him, she assumes his faith must have been false, otherwise He would surely have saved him during his lifetime.

39. Also, because she does not feel her punishment immediately, she thinks there is no longer any seriousness in it. She does not know that the longer she waits, the more she encloses herself in folly and becomes a powerful source <note>original: *Quall*; a term used by Böhme to describe both a "source/fountain" and the "torment/agony" arising from it</note> of eternal pain within herself. When the light of outer nature—in which she prided herself in her **egoism** <term>Ichheit: "I-ness" or the state of being centered entirely on the self</term> for a time—is broken, she then stands within herself in eternal darkness and agony, finding that her false, selfish desire is a vain, rough, prickly, and hard sharpness and resentment.

40. During this time, she hopes for external help and leads herself into the pleasures of her own will, considering that to be her kingdom of heaven. But when the outer light is extinguished in death, she then stands in eternal despair and sees no savior around or within her.

Thus, he powerfully demonstrated how the eternal One can rule mightily over multiplicity and self-interest—showing that the power of formed things <term>Bildlichkeit: the world of images, forms, and created things</term> is not a God, but that the power of that which is beyond and without form rules everything. This grace has pressed upon all people through One (the first man), according to Romans 5:18. One must accept this grace and, in the power of such acceptance and divine union, sink oneself with a yielded <note>original: *gelassenen*; referring to the state of "Gelassenheit" or total resignation of the self to God</note> life-will into the supersensible, unfathomable, eternal One, as into the first ground of life’s beginning. 23. New Rebirth, or the Divine Will, becomes active or manifest in such a life; and such a person (as long as he stands in the earthly will alone) is no child of heaven. For the **Divine Science** <term>Göttliche Scienz: Böhme uses this to mean the innate divine pattern, wisdom, or "formative knowledge" that directs creation</term> is turned into an earthly, beastly quality through the **self-shaping** <note>original: *Selb-Bildung*; refers to the soul creating its own ego-driven identity rather than letting God shape it</note> of the false will. 24. He scatters not only the Divine order of the senses, but he also sows his works into a false ground.

25. Consider a **parable** <note>original: *Gleichniß*</note> of the sun: When a plant has no sap, the sun’s ray burns it; but if it has sap, the sun’s ray warms it, causing it to grow. It is the same in the life of the **essence** <note>original: *Essenz*</note> in man: If that life does not have the **Ens** <term>Ens: a Latin term for "being" or "entity"; for Böhme, it represents the spiritual substance or "food" that gives the soul its character</term> of God’s gentleness and love—flowing from the eternal One—then it compresses itself into a fierce, fiery sharpness. The **mind** <term>Gemüth: the seat of the soul's inclinations and emotions</term> becomes entirely rough, hungry, greedy, envious, and prickly. And such a false sense and will later passes from the inner life into the body, and into all the person's being and works.

26. Thus, such a firing, greedy, and envious nature, with its sharp **sense** <note>original: *Sensu*</note> of life, scatters and breaks everything that is good. In everything it deals with, there is **peril** <note>original: *Fährlichkeit*</note>; for it drives its venomous rays into everything, seeking to pull everything to itself and inject its poison like a hungry spirit. But if it happens that this fiery life can "eat" of Divine Love, it becomes a likeness of how light breaks forth and proceeds from a fire. In this way, the true life breaks through from the "firing" nature with a new spirit and a will of Divine Love from within. It is no longer "taking," as is the nature of fire, but "giving." For the will of Love gives of itself, just as light flows from fire, giving itself into all things and working a "good" in everything.

->### IX. Path to Christ.<-

27. If the sun, in the depths of the world, no longer shone, then the **Spirit of the World** <term>Spiritus Mundi: the animating spirit or "soul" of the physical universe</term>—within the harshness of the stars and the **Sulfurous** and **Mercurial** <note>original: *Sulphurischen, Mercurialischen*; Böhme uses these alchemical terms to describe the fundamental energies of contraction/fire and expansion/motion</note> qualities of the four elements—would become entirely severe, raw, dry, bitter, thick, dark, and hard. Thus all life in the elements would perish, and one would soon see what Hell and **GOD’S** wrath truly are.

28. Likewise, just as the outer man is an **extract** <term>Limus: literally "slime" or "mud," referring to the biblical creation of man from the dust of the ground</term> of the outer elemental world, whose life consists in the power of the sun and stars, and just as the body (as well as the earth) is a **solidification** <note>original: *Coagulation*</note> of the **Spirit of the World**; if it could not have the sun’s light-love-power in its **nourishment** <note>original: *Nutrimento*</note>, it would become entirely evil, fiery, and deadly, and the outer life would necessarily perish.

29. In the very same way, the soul is an **extract** from the inner spiritual world, coming out of the **Great Mystery** <term>Mysterio Magno: the chaos or "Great Abyss" from which God brings forth the manifestation of all things</term>, as an emergence and **reflection** <note>original: *Gegenwurf*; literally a "counter-throw," suggesting the soul is a mirror or manifestation of Divine knowledge</note> of Divine Science, and it must take its **nourishment** from that same **Great Mystery** of Divine power and science. If it happens that the soul does not desire the **Essence** <term>Ens: a Latin term for "being" or "entity"; here it refers to the spiritual substance the soul "eats"</term> of Divine Love for its food, and if it breaks itself away from the **Abyss** <term>Ungrund: the "Groundless," God's primal state before manifestation</term>—that is, away from **yieldedness** <note>original: *Gelassenheit*; the state of surrendering one’s self-will to God</note>—then the soul becomes harsh, fiery, dark, raw, prickly, envious, hostile, rebellious, and a total unrest unto itself. It leads itself into a deadly, dying, fierce torment, which is its damnation, wherein it withers just as happened to the devil, and as happens to all the godless.

30. But if such a **fire-torment** <note>original: *Feuer-Quall*; Böhme often puns on "Qual" (torment) and "Quelle" (source), suggesting the soul's inner fire is both its source of life and its source of pain</note> can again reach Divine Love as the essential light of **GOD** and receive it into itself, then such a soul-fire-torment is transformed into a kingdom of joy and into the praise of **GOD**. But without a turned-around will—one that can stand still and cease its own **drawing-in** <note>original: *Impression*; refers to the soul's egoistic "grasping" or "compressing" of itself</note> and enclosure—this is not possible. For the light of the sun cannot work within a hard stone in the same way it works in metals, herbs, and trees, because the water within the stone is caught and **solidified** in a hard **compression**.

31. This is also how the false self-will of the soul is to be understood in relation to Divine gentleness: that the Divine gentleness, within such a greedy, envious fire-desire...

### Chapter 3, 6. Of Divine Contemplation.

-> The Word was with God, and God was the Word; the same was in the beginning with God: All things were made through the same; and without the same nothing was made that was made. <note>A translation of John 1:1–3, the foundational scripture for this chapter's argument.</note> <-

1. The beginning of all beings has been the Word, as the out-breathing of God; and God has been the eternal One from eternity, and remains so into eternity. But the Word is the outflow of the Divine Will or the Divine knowledge <note>original: *Wissenschaft*, which in this context means a conscious, structured knowledge rather than modern academic science</note>. Just as the senses flow out from the mind, yet the mind is only one single thing; so also has the eternal One been present within the outflow of the Will. This is what is meant by: **In the beginning was the WORD.** For the Word, as the outflow from the Will of God, has been the eternal beginning and remains so eternally. For it is the revelation of the eternal One, by which and through which the Divine power is brought into a knowledge of "Something" <term>Ichts: a term coined by Böhme to represent "somethingness" or "aught," the opposite of "Nichts" (nothing)</term>. And by the **WORD**, we understand the manifest Will of God; and by the Word of **GOD**, we understand the hidden God, as the eternal One from which the Word eternally springs.

4. From such a revelation of powers, in which the Will of the Eternal One beholds itself, there flows out the understanding and the knowledge of the "Something" <gloss>Ichts</gloss>, wherein the eternal Will beholds itself in the "Something," and leads itself into a desire within Wisdom toward a likeness and image.

He is the distinctness within the Will, from which powers and properties originate.

...the Separator has signed <note>original: *signiret*. This refers to Böhme’s "Signature of All Things," the belief that the inner spiritual essence of a thing is marked upon its outward physical form.</note> and made visible, as can be recognized in all life.

16. The innermost foundation is a spark of the out-flowed Will of **God**, through the eternal breathing of **God**, and is united with **God’s WORD**, to will nothing else than only what the one Will of **God** wills through such an outflow.

17. It is the Separator <term>Separator: the "Divider" or "Distinguisher"—the demiurgic power that differentiates the divine unity into specific, physical forms.</term> of the Divine Will, as an instrument of **God**, into which the Divine Will has formed itself into a wonder-worker of omnipotence and glory, with which He intends to rule all things; for this reason, divine understanding has also been given to it.

### Chapter 3. 6. On Divine Contemplation.

The visible being does not receive the invisible into a state of possession or its own power, as if the outer might thereby be transformed into the inner; No, that is not the case. The inner power only forms itself with the outer, just as we understand the powers of herbs, trees, and metals: that their outward spirit is merely a tool of the inner spirit, acting as the inner power, through which the inner power forms itself into the outer spirit.

20. Since we then understand three kinds of **spirit** <note>original: *Spiritus*</note> in such powers of growing things, which exist in different **centers** <note>original: *Centris*</note> and yet in only one **body** <note>original: *Corpore*</note>. The first and outermost **spirit** is the coarse **Sulfur, Salt, and Mercury** <note>original: *Schwefel, Saltz und Mercurius*. In Böhme’s alchemy, these represent the fundamental spiritual qualities: Sulfur is the fiery source of life, Salt is the stabilizing form, and Mercury is the fluid movement or communication between them.</note>. This is a being of the four **elements** or of the **stars** <note>original: *Gestirnes*</note>, according to the harsh quality of the stars. This spirit creates the **body** <note>original: *Corpus*</note> and impresses itself, or takes form as a being, or draws the inner from the spiritual **Separator** <term>Separator: the "Divider"—the power that distinguishes the unified divine essence into specific physical forms.</term> into itself, as well as the **elements** from the outside, and **coagulates** <note>original: *coaguliret*—the process of turning spirit or liquid into solid matter.</note> with them. From this, the **Signature** <note>original: *Signatur*—the outward mark or appearance that reveals a thing's inner character.</note> or designation immediately occurs through the **Separator**. This same spirit forms the visible **body** according to the quality of the greatest power of the **World Spirit** <note>original: *Spiritus Mundi*—the animating soul of the physical universe.</note>, such as the **constellation** of the stars, or the quality of the **planets** and the currently ignited **elements**.

21. The second **spirit**, which has its own **center**, lies in the **oil** of the **sulfur**, which is called the **fifth essence** <note>original: *5te Essenz*—the Quintessence, the purest and most refined element that serves as the root and life-force of the four physical elements.</note>, acting as a root of the four **elements**. This is the softening and joy of the coarse, painful **sulfur** and **salt-spirit**. It takes its **nourishment** <note>original: *Nutriment*</note> first from within, from the light of nature—as an outflow of spiritual gentleness from the inner spiritual fire and light. And secondly, from the outside, it takes its **nourishment** from the sun and from the subtle power of the **World Spirit**, and is the true cause of growing life, a joy of nature, just as the sun is within the **elements**.

22. The third **spirit** is the **Tincture** <note>original: *Tinctur*—the highest spiritual essence or "color" that brings things to their ultimate perfection.</note>, acting as a counter-projection <term>Gegenwurf: an object or reflection through which the Divine Will views itself.</term> of the Divine **Great Mystery** <note>original: *Mysterii Magni*—the unmanifested potential of God.</note>, where all powers lie in equality. It is rightly called **Paradise** or Divine Delight. It is a housing of Divine power, a housing of eternal souls, from which all outer powers spring forth, in the same way that air arises from fire.

### Chapter 3. 6. On Divine Contemplation.

46. But that which is hard and compressing—such as bone, wood, herbs, metals, fire, earth, stones, and similar materials—within these lies the image of Divine power and movement. But in thinness <note>meaning fluidity or subtlety</note>, it does not lie in such sensitivity, but is equal to all things—just as water and air are equal to all things and are in all things. But the "dry water" is the true **pearl-ground** <note>original: *Perlen-Grund*—the alchemical or spiritual substrate from which the "pearl" of divine wisdom or the philosopher's stone emerges</note>, wherein the subtle power of the Unity's working lies in the center. Physicians <note>original: *Medicis*</note> should take careful note of this: they should not look only at the coarse spirits <note>original: *Spiritus*—referring here to volatile vapors or chemical spirits</note> of strong odor and mistake them for the true healing essence <term>balsam: the life-preserving fluid or principle that prevents decay and promotes health</term>. 49. The spirits of strong power found in the odor must be brought into the balanced state <note>original: *Temperamentum*</note>, that is, into unity, and not allowed to fly away. Otherwise, one seeks to cure with salt—acting as the sharpness of fire—and administers the soul to the patient without the spirit.

50. The soul of such healing essences is divided in its properties; each part gives of itself in its own great joy individually, but in this state of separation, they are too resistant. They do not unify the enmity and division of life, but rather they ignite the division of life even further.

51. To provoke things to wrath only creates pride and strife, which can be seen in all things.

52. A prisoner is comforted only by the thought of his release, until he places his will in hope and composes himself with patience; finally, his restlessness falls into hope, into the balanced state <note>original: *Temperamentum*</note>, and in such hope, he learns to become humble. If one then speaks to him of his release, he rejoices.

53. So it is with you, Physicians; mark this well, for this is your pearl, if you are able to understand it: the meaning is both internal and external.

Chapter 4. 6. Of Divine Contemplation.

...world created, and for what purpose the creaturely ground <term>creaturely ground: the fundamental essence or "soil" of a created being's nature</term> is useful? Also to what end joy and sorrow have been made manifest? and how God is so near to all things?

### Summaries.

The Eternal Word has come into that which has flowed forth, §. 1. 2. but the turned-away will did not receive it. 3. But to whichever will turned itself back toward the New Birth, to that one He gave power to become God’s child. 4. The inner ground has made itself visible. 5.

1. In John 1: 11-13 it is written: HE (JESUS CHRIST) came into his own <note>original: *Eigenthum*—meaning his own property or domain</note>, and his own received Him not; but as many as received Him, to them gave He power to become the children of God, who believe in his name: which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.

2. In these words lies the precious ground of Divine Revelation, described as the Eternal Inwardness and Out-going <note>original: *Ewige Ein und Aus*</note>: For they speak of how the hidden Divine Eternal WORD—the Divine power of unity—has come OUT into the out-flowed, natural, creaturely, figurative WORD <note>By "figurative word," the author means the visible world, which acts as a symbol or "image" of God's internal speech</note>, as into humanity, coming into its own property.

3. For the out-flowed, figurative, creaturely WORD is the property of the Eternally-speaking WORD; and it is clearly indicated thereby, that His own—meaning the turned-away, figurative, self-serving will—did not receive Him; which self-centered, figurative will had arisen from its own ground, as from the flesh and blood of its own nature, from man and woman. That is to say, it arose in the Separator <note>original: *Separatore*—the principle of differentiation that divides the unity of God into the many forms of nature</note> of the out-flowed will, where the eternal will had closed itself off into self-ownership, and wanted to GO OUT and rule in its own strength and power.

4. This [self-will] did not receive the Eternal WORD, which, as an outflow of Divine grace, came OUT again to the turned-away will, because it wanted to be its own master; but to whichever will turned itself back, so that it might be born-anew in the Divine outflow of love, to that one He gave power to [be] God’s child

is the temperament <note>original: *temperamentum*—in Böhme's thought, this refers to a state of perfect balance or equilibrium where all opposing qualities of nature are harmonized</note>, wherein the distinctness of all powers lies back within [unity]. 50. The soul of such balsams is divided in its qualities; each gives itself in its own great joy particularly, but in this separation they are too contrary: they do not unite the enmity and division of life, but rather they kindle the division of life even more.

52. A prisoner is only comforted by his release, until he sets his will in hope and composes himself with patience; thus his unrest finally falls through hope into the temperament, and he learns to become humble in such hope. When he is then told of his release, he rejoices.

53. Therefore you physicians, mark this: that is your pearl, if you can understand this; the meaning is both inward and outward.

A poor soul had wandered out of Paradise and had come into the kingdom of this world; there the devil met her and said to her: "Where are you going, you half-blind soul?"

2. The soul said: "I want to behold the creatures of the world which the Creator has made."

3. The devil said: "How will you behold them, since you cannot recognize what essence and quality they are? <note>original: "Essenz und Eigenschaft." 4. The soul said: "How might I then know them in their essence and being?"

5. The devil said: "If you eat of that from which the creatures, both Good and Evil, are made, then your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God Himself, and know what the Creator is."

6. The soul said: "I am noble and holy, and might die from that, as the Creator has spoken."

# IX. The Way to Christ.

22. The soul did as the devil advised, yet did not recognize him as the devil; instead, she thought it was her own cleverness and reason, and that she was doing well and right.

23. While she was thus running along in such a lifestyle, she was one day met by our dear Lord Jesus Christ with God's love and wrath. He had come into this world to destroy the works of the devil and to hold judgment over all godless works. He told her she should turn back and <term>repent</term> <note>original: "Busse thun." 24. When this occurred, and the spark of Divine Light became manifest within her, she looked at herself along with her works and her will. She became aware that she stood in Hell within the wrath of God, and recognized that she was a phantom-mask and a monster before God and the kingdom of heaven. She was so greatly terrified by this that the greatest anxiety awoke within her, for the judgment of God was made manifest in her.

25. When this happened, the Lord Christ spoke to her with his voice of grace: Repent and leave vanity behind, and you shall come to my grace.

26. The soul stepped before God in her mask-like image, wearing the soiled garment of vanity, and pleaded for grace, that God would forgive her sins. They also feared the mockery of the world if they should leave their worldly honor and glory. ### 7th Dialogue of an Enlightened and Unenlightened Soul.

...take **Heaven**; such plucking, awakening, and grieving as you do now is not necessary.

37. In such and similar thoughts, the **soul** was imprisoned by the **devil** in the **lust of the flesh** and **earthly will**, bound as if with great chains. It did not know what to do; it thought perhaps of returning to the world and its pleasures, and yet found within itself a great hunger for **Divine grace**, and always wanted to enter into **repentance** and come to **God's** favor. For the hand of **God** had touched and shattered it: therefore it could find rest nowhere, but groaned within itself for remorse over committed sins, and wanted to be free of them, yet could not reach any right, true repentance, much less the recognition of sins; and yet it stood in such hunger and desire for remorse and repentance.

38. It therefore resolved to go to a lonely place and turn away from business. It also thought it would bind itself to charity toward the poor <note>The soul mistakenly believes that "good works" or physical isolation can earn salvation, a common stage of spiritual struggle in Böhme's theology.</note> so that **God** might be merciful to it, and sought all kinds of ways to its rest, how it might come to favor and grace.

39. For it felt the awakened **wrath of God** <note>original: "Grimm GOttes". # IX. The Way to Christ.

40. ...hold of the first movement of grace, and she did not know that **Christ** stood in her hell, within **God's** wrath and strict justice, and was fighting with the embodied **Satan** and the spirit of delusion in both her soul and body. She did not understand that such hunger and desire for **repentance** and **conversion** came from **Christ** Himself—that she was being drawn in this way. Furthermore, she did not know what she still lacked, or why she could not reach a state of **Divine sensitivity** <note>This refers to a conscious, felt awareness of God's presence.</note>. She did not know that she was monstrous <note>Böhme uses "monstrous" to describe the soul's distorted state after the Fall, where it has lost its original divine shape.</note> and wore a **serpent-image** upon her, through which the **devil** had such power and access to her, and in which he had confused all her good senses and led them away from **God**. Of this, **Christ** said: *The devil snatches the word from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.* Luke 8:12.

41. By **God's** providence, this poor, troubled **soul** once met a **soul** enlightened by **God** and born anew, who spoke to her: "What is the matter with you, troubled **soul**, that you are so restless and stand in such sorrow?"

42. The troubled **soul** said: "The **Creator** has hidden His face from me, so that I cannot come to His rest; therefore I am so sorrowful and know not what I should do to obtain His favor. For mountains and great chasms lie between me and His favor, so that I cannot come to Him, no matter how much I yearn for Him; I am held back so that I cannot reach His power, even though I worry about it and wait for Him with longing desire."

43. The enlightened **soul** spoke to her: "You carry upon you a masked image of the **devil**, which looks like the **serpent**, and you are surrounded by it. Within it, the **devil** has access to you, as if it were your own property, and there he holds back your **will** so that it cannot penetrate into **God**. Otherwise, if your **will** were to penetrate into **God**, it would be anointed with the highest power of **God** in the resurrection of our Lord **Jesus Christ**. Then that **anointing** <term>Salbung: the spiritual infusion of grace that heals and transforms the soul</term> would shatter the monster within you, and your original **Paradisical image** would again be revealed in you. Then the **devil** would lose his power over you, and you would become an **angel** once more. And because he begrudges you this, he keeps you imprisoned in his desire within your **fleshly lusts**."

### 7. Dialogue between an Enlightened and an Unenlightened Soul.

...and if you do not become free from this, then you are separated from **God**, and will never enter into our company.

44. At this speech, the poor, troubled **soul** was so terrified that she could no longer speak a word; for she heard that she bore the **serpent-image** <note>original: "Schlangen Bild." In Jacob Böhme’s mystical theology, this refers to the distorted, selfish nature of humanity after the Fall, which mimics the cunning and earthly desires of the serpent.</note> upon her, which separated her from **God**. She realized that the **devil** was so near to her within it, mixing his will into her false thoughts, and that he held such power over her. She felt herself so close to **damnation** and standing in the abyss of **hell**, imprisoned in **God's** wrath, and she was ready to despair of **God's grace**.

45. But the power of her **shattering** <note>original: "Zerschellung." This refers to "contrition" or the spiritual breaking of the ego and self-will, which Böhme sees as a necessary step for rebirth.</note> held her so that she did not despair; instead, she wrestled within herself between hope and doubt. Whatever hope built up, doubt tore down again. She remained in constant unrest, so much so that ultimately the world with all its beauty became a **vanity** (a source of disgust) to her, and she no longer wished to enjoy any worldly pleasure, yet she could find no rest.

46. After a time, the **enlightened soul** came to her again and found her in such agonies, and said to her: "What is it you are doing? Do you wish to burst apart in your anxieties? Why do you torment yourself in your own power and will, since you are but a worm? Your torment only grows greater because of it. Indeed, even if you were to sink yourself into the depths of the sea, or try to fly to the **dawn** <note>original: "Morgenröthe." A significant term for Böhme (as in his work *Aurora*), representing the first light of divine wisdom breaking through the darkness of the soul.</note>, or soar above the stars, you would still not be free. For the more you agonize yourself, the greater and more painful your nature becomes, and yet you do not come to rest; for your own ability is entirely lost. Just as a dried-up **cabbage** <note>original: "Kohl." Used here as a metaphor for a withered plant or stalk that has lost its life-giving sap.</note> cannot turn green or gain sap again through its own power so that it might rejoice again with the trees; so too you cannot reach the place of **God** through your own power, nor transform yourself back into your first **angelic form**. For you have withered and died away from **God**, like the plant has lost its strength and sap. You are nothing but an anxious, dry hunger; your qualities are like heat and cold which stand in conflict and can never become one."

# IX. Way to Christ.

...that I might turn green again, and receive my first life, in which I stood in peace before I was an image? <note>original: "Bilde." Böhme refers to the soul's original state in God before it became a separate, self-willed entity or "image" focused on the material world.</note>

48. **The enlightened soul spoke:** You should do nothing except abandon your own will and your own self-satisfaction; then your evil qualities will all grow weak and venture toward death. Thus, with your will, you will sink back into the **One** <note>original: "das Eine." This refers to the "Unground" or the primal unity of God, a central concept in Böhme’s mysticism where all conflict ceases.</note> from which you originated in the beginning. For you now lie imprisoned within the **creatures** <term>creatures: in Böhme’s vocabulary, "creatures" (Creaturen) refers to all created, worldly things and the selfish desires the soul has for them.</term>; so when your will leaves them, the creatures—with their evil inclinations that currently hold you back from coming to **God**—will die within you.

49. And if you do this, **God** will send His highest love to meet you, which He revealed in the humanity of **Christ JESUS**. This love will give you sap and life again, so that you turn green once more and rejoice with the living of **God**. <note>Böhme frequently uses botanical metaphors like "sap" and "turning green" to describe the organic, living process of spiritual regeneration.</note> You will also receive the **image of God** again and be rid of this **serpent-image**; then you will join our **angelic host** and become my brother.

50. **The poor soul spoke:** How shall I leave my own will so that the creatures within it might die, since I live in the world and must have the world?

51. **The enlightened soul spoke:** Currently, you hold temporal honor and wealth, along with the **lust of the flesh**, as your own property; you think little of what you do within them or how you draw them to yourself. Even when you see the wretched suffer in need—who is nonetheless your brother—you do not rescue him; instead, you bind him and torment him by seizing his work and toil for yourself and delighting in it. Moreover, you are stubborn and proud in this, exalting yourself against him and regarding him as nothing compared to you.

52. Thus, the wretched one stands and sighs toward **God** because his labor is taken from him and he must live in misery beside you. With his sighing, he awakens **God’s wrath** within you, which makes your flame and unrest ever greater.

53. And these are your **creatures** that you love, and for whose sake you have broken yourself off from **God**, and your...

### IX. Way to Christ.

...to be firmly imprinted with the **Lord Jesus Christ**, and to sink yourself into Him with all your reason and senses, desiring to remain therein forever, and desiring to die away to your **creatures** <note>In Böhme’s theology, "creatures" refers to the selfish, worldly impulses like pride and greed that take form within the soul.</note> within Him.

59. Furthermore, you must firmly resolve to turn your **desire** and **mind** away from all false attachments, and not allow temporal honor or goods to hold you; you must also put away from you whatever is wrong and what might hinder you; your will must be entirely pure, and directed in such a sincere resolution that you never again wish to enter back into your false **creatures**, but rather leave them at that very hour and separate your mind from them, intending at that very hour to step upon the pure way of **truth** and **righteousness**, and to follow the teaching of **Christ**.

60. And just as you now intend to leave the enemies of your own nature, so must you also yourself forgive all your external enemies, and intend to meet them with your **love**, so that there may not perhaps be any creature that can take hold of your **will** and restrain you, but that it may become pure of every creature.

61. You must also be willing to gladly leave all your temporal honor and goods for **Christ's** sake, if that should be required, and not wish to take up anything that is earthly to love it, but rather consider yourself in your station and temporal honors and goods only as a **servant of God** and of your fellow Christians, as a **steward of God** in your office: the **high eyes of self-love** <note>This refers to the "pride" mentioned on the previous page—the tendency to look down on others or focus on one's own ego.</note> must be broken and humbled, so that no creatures remain within them which might lead the senses into mental images.

62. In addition, you should firmly believe <term>imprint within yourself<gloss>einbilden</gloss></term> <note>The German term "einbilden" here is a technical term for Böhme, meaning to literally form an image or "incarnate" a spiritual reality within the soul through the power of the will.</note> that you will certainly attain the promised **grace** in the merit of **Jesus Christ**, as His outflowing love, which will redeem you from those creatures, and enlighten your will, and ignite it with the **flame of love**, whereby you will become victorious against the **Devil**.

63. Not that you could or would do anything by your own power, but you should imprint the **suffering and resurrection of Christ** upon yourself, and take it into yourself as your own property, and with it intend to [withstand] the **Devil**...

...[He will] break and storm His kingdom in you, and kill your **creatures** <note>In Böhme’s theology, "creatures" refers to the selfish, worldly impulses and mental constructs that belong to the "fallen" self rather than to God.</note>. And you should make such a resolution to enter into this at this very hour, and never wish to depart from it eternally, but rather wish to surrender your will in all its beginnings and deeds to **God**, so that He may work with you and do with you what He wills.

64. Now, if your will and resolution are thus prepared, it has broken through your **creatures** and stands purely before **God**, clothed with the merit of **Jesus Christ**. Now it may come to the Father with the **prodigal son** <note>A reference to the parable in Luke 15, where a wandering son returns home to his father's mercy.</note>, and fall down before His face, and pour out its confession before Him, and put all its strength into this working, and confess its sin and disobedience, along with its turning away from **God**—not with mere words, but with all its strength: which is yet only such a resolution, for the soul of itself is capable of nothing.

65. 66. And here is now the right place where you may wrestle in such a divine gaze; if you stand firm here and do not depart from it, you will see and experience great wonders. For you will experience within yourself how **Christ** will storm **hell** <note>Böhme describes "hell" not just as a place, but as the dark, chaotic state of the soul separated from God's light.</note> in you, and break your **beasts** <note>The "beasts" (*Thiere*) represent the various animalistic passions—like greed, envy, or anger—that dominate the unregenerate human mind.</note>, which will cause an uproar and misery to arise in you; and how your previously unrecognized sin will first wake up in you and want to separate you from **God** and hold you back; and you will truly experience how death and life struggle with one another, and you will experience what **heaven** and **hell** are.

67. At this you should not be offended, but stand firm and not depart; then finally all your evil **beasts** will become weary and weak, and venture to die; then...

Then it thought within itself: you are not purely surrendered to **God**, you wish to ask or desire nothing from **God**, but rather surrender yourself to His judgment, so that He may kill your evil self-will; you wish to sink yourself to the very bottom, outside all nature and creature, into Him, and surrender yourself to Him, so that He may do with you as He wills, for you are not worthy to speak to Him. ### IX. Way to Christ.

74. Then the Slanderer <note>original: *Läſterer*; here referring to the Devil as the "accuser" or "tempter"</note> approached her and wanted to ruin this way for her and lead her into doubt, and whispered into her: "It is not from God; it has only been your imagination."

75. The Divine Light also withdrew from her and glowed only in the inner ground <term>inner ground: *inwendigen Grunde*, a mystical term for the deepest part of the soul where the human meets the Divine</term> like a smoldering fire, so that reason saw itself as entirely foolish and forsaken. She did not know what was happening to her, or whether it was certainly true that she had tasted the Divine Light of Grace, and yet she could not let go of it.

76. For the fire-burning love of God had been sown in her, through which a great hunger and thirst for Divine Sweetness <note>a common mystical metaphor for the experiential joy of God's presence</note> arose within her. She then began truly to pray, to humble herself before God, to examine her evil inclinations <gloss>original: *Neiglichkeit*; the natural tendency toward sin</gloss> in her thoughts, and to reject them.

77. Through this, the will of her reason was broken, and the evil innate inclination was killed more and more. This caused great pain to the nature of the body, which fell into a faintness like a sickness; yet it was no natural sickness, but rather a melancholy <note>original: *Melancholia*; used here to describe the physical and emotional "heaviness" that occurs when earthly desires are denied</note> of the body's earthly nature, because its false pleasure had been broken.

78. 79. In such contemplation, the Enlightened Soul met her again and spoke to her: "What is the matter with you, my brother, that you are so sad?"

All fear and sadness is from the soul, §. 1. because it is held in a dark dungeon by the spirit of this world. ibid.
This [spirit] has 4 lodgings, 2. namely choleric, 3. sanguine, 4. phlegmatic 5. and melancholic. 6:8. In one of these housings the soul lies captive, 9. and one dwells within the other. 10. God’s Spirit does not enter into the fire. 22.

All sadness and fear, where man is horrified within himself and is afraid, is from the soul. For the external spirit from the stars and elements is not horrified, since it lives in its mother <note>Nature or the physical world.</note> who gave birth to it: But the poor soul has entered into a foreign lodging with Adam, namely into the spirit of this world; there the beautiful creature is covered up and held in a dark dungeon.

IX. Way to Christ.

2. Now, the spirit of this world has four lodgings in which that noble jewel <note>The "jewel" refers to the human soul or the inner divine spark.</note> stands imprisoned. Among these four, one is primarily manifest in a person, and not all four at once; this is according to the four elements that every person has within themselves. Man is himself that same essence, with the exception of the soul, which is not of that same essence but lies captured within it. Yet the soul has only one lodging or configuration among the four that holds the chief rule over its life. These four are called (1) Choleric, (2) Sanguine, (3) Phlegmatic, and (4) Melancholic.

3. (1) **Choleric** is of the nature and property of Fire; it gives strong courage, sudden anger, the rising of pride, stubbornness, and heeding no one. This configuration appears, according to the outward world, in a fire-light; it works according to the power of the Sun and always desires to be the master.

4. (2) **Sanguine**, according to the Air, is subtle, friendly, and cheerful, yet not of strong courage. It is changeable and easily moved from one thing to another. It naturally receives the property and wit <note>In this context, "wit" (Wiß) refers to mental capacity or natural intelligence.</note> of the stars into its essence; it is modest and pure, and carries great secrecy in its knowledge.

5. (3) **Phlegmatic** is according to the nature and property of Water; it is fleshy, coarse, and soft, of a womanly <note>In the 17th century, "womanly" (weibisch) was often used as a technical term for a receptive or "soft" psychological state, rather than a literal comment on gender.</note> will and moderate understanding. However, it holds fast to what it receives. Knowledge must be brought into it through sound and teaching; it does not discover it from its own root. It lets everything be as it is and does not fall into melancholy; it has a glimmer of light, being neither sad nor highly joyful, but takes everything easily and commonly.

6. (4) **Melancholic** is of the nature and property of the Earth; like the earth, it is cold, rigid, dark, sad, and hungry for the light, always fearful of God’s wrath.

7. For the earth and stones are outside the eternal essence; that is, they were seized in the ignited desire in the **Fiat** <note>original: "Fiat"; the Latin command "Let it be done," referring to the divine act of creation.</note> according to the property of wrath as well as love. There is both evil and good mixed together. The good always has a fear of the evil; it is a constant fleeing. The good always wants to flee from the evil, as can be seen in metals, where the **tincture** <note>original: "Tinctur"; an alchemical term for the spiritual essence or life-force that gives a substance its quality.</note> is good, and the purely earthly part is evil and fierce. There, the tincture of the metals always wants to [flee] from the earthly—

<header>8. Consolatory Treatise on the Four Complexions. 227</header>

## 1. The Choleric Complexion according to Fire.

23. If the soul-life is surrounded by the **Choleric Complexion** <term>complexion: a person’s natural temperament or "humor" (choleric, sanguine, phlegmatic, or melancholic), believed in the 17th century to be governed by the four elements</term>, it is fiery, fierce, rising, and consuming. It also produces a body that is lean, malicious, fierce, and angry; and when the soul **imagines** <note>original: "imaginiret"—for Böhme, this refers to the soul's ability to focus its desire and "image" its reality into being</note> into it, it ignites the temperament even more, for the soul is also fiery. From this, there arises in man anger, pride, and a desire to rise in power and pomp, to suppress everything beneath him, to mock the wretched, and to rule over those on bended knees. He cares nothing if someone dies in his anger—unless the **stars** <note>original: "Gestirne"—Böhme believed the alignment of the heavens influenced human behavior and could sometimes temper a person's natural rage</note> prevent it, which often intervene and hinder much through a combination of temperaments.

24. Great danger exists in this temperament if the soul lives in external imagination; it is held in a hard bond when one fire-torment is bound to another.

25. The fierce Devil has a powerful entrance to this soul, for the property of fire serves him. He is also proud and envious, just as this temperament is. Oh, how difficult it is for the soul to get loose once it is properly ignited in this property! The Devil does not even need to tempt it; it follows his tune quite willingly. It does not easily become sad, for it possesses a "fire-light" in its temperament and constantly thinks it is God’s light and that it is on the right path. Yet, it remains a proud, envious, angry, powerful, and oppressive will and spirit so long as the soul relies only on its temperament. Oh, it gladly gives off a glistening appearance in its pomp, drawn from its fire-complexion and radiance; in its great pride and arrogance, it even wants to be praised as holy. Oh, Devil in an **angel's form** <note>A reference to 2 Corinthians 11:14, warning that evil can mask itself as divine light</note>, how dark you will be when the temperament breaks apart in death!

Everything the **stars** <note>original: "Gestirn"—referring to the astrological influences that Böhme believed shaped the physical body and personality</note> produce, the soul experiences within the **temperament** <term>complexion: the "humor" or physical constitution of a person</term>; it is joyful, yet soon discouraged before the power of fire (as if before **great lords** <note>original: "grossen Hansen"—an idiom for people of high status or "big shots"</note>), but within itself it is powerful in its own mind, without need of counsel. It possesses sharp reason through the temperament according to the external spirit; it does not easily do anything harmful in anger; it is now uplifting and high-minded, and then falling again, just like the air. It must be on guard, for the Devil is hostile toward it. He cannot affect it much within the temperament itself, but he would like to confuse it so that it might entertain many different senses, preventing it from **imagining** <note>original: "imaginiren"—to focus the soul's desire and creative power</note> toward God's kingdom. He places strange things before it to pass its time; it likes to study many things, for the stars cast their imagination into the air, from which the soul receives many strange, rambling thoughts.

28. Such a person leads a weak, common, pious, and simple life, but the Devil excellently stirs up his enemies against him; he must suffer much, yet he passes through it easily, just as air passes through something. He is rarely very sad, for he does not carry a fiery heart, and thus terror does not burn harshly within him. Yet he must guard against unchastity and idolatry, for through these the Devil gains an entrance into the temperament.

### 3. The Phlegmatic Complexion according to Water.

29. If the soul is surrounded by this temperament and breathes its life from it, it is a thick, swollen life—clumsy, almost base, and of little account. It has a coarse body and poor reason, yet through teaching, all common knowledge can be brought into it. If the power of the Moon does not intervene, it is a truly coarse lump, and even then, it is almost unjust through the Moon's power.

30. One can carve anything out of this temperament; the water-spirit takes on everything, now evil, now good. It likes to present itself as a holy hypocrite and attributes to itself a pious, righteous life, but it is a mixture. The water is **deceptive** <note>original: "scheinlich"—appearing to be something it is not; shiny but shallow</note>; the soul does not easily become aware of God's wrath or the dark world (which is at its center). It bites greedily at the abominations of the world and hides them under a watery shimmer, believing it to be God's radiance.

### 4. The Melancholic Temperament according to the Earth.

32. The Melancholic Temperament resembles the sad earth, which stands always in fear of the **Wrath of God** <note>original: "Grimm GOttes"—in Böhme's thought, the "Grimm" is the harsh, dark, and consuming quality of the first principle of nature</note> that entered into it during the Creation; it provides a moderate understanding, yet is somewhat deeply meditative.

33. The chamber of this temperament stands open; much may be grasped within it, provided that **melancholy** <term>Schwermuth: literally "heavy spirit" or deep depression</term> does not hinder it. If the soul is surrounded by this temperament so that it "eats" from it, its fire-burning becomes almost dark and very sad; it holds no worldly luxury in high regard, and through the temperament it is always heavy-spirited and fearful like the earth. The Devil attacks it harshly, for he would always like to plunge it completely into the darkness, into his kingdom.

34. For where it is dark, he gladly enters; he creates **images** <note>original: "Fürbilde"—mental representations or illusions</note> for the soul and terrifies it with his **malice** <term>Schalckheit: wickedness or deceptive craftiness</term> so that it might despair of God's grace. For the soul in this chamber of melancholy does not otherwise bring much that is useful to him—unless it should despair of God's grace and become entirely reckless. In that case, the body can produce a murderer and a robber who regards man, God, and the Devil all as equal. For if the soul despairs and gives itself over to whatever the temperament does with it, then this person does everything that the stars work within the temperament, and the Devil mixes his **imagination** <note>original: "Imagination"—for Böhme, this is the soul's creative and attractive power to "form" its own reality</note> into it.

### 8. Treatise on Consolation regarding the 4 Temperaments 235

He is not worth the effort; simply fix this one little verse in your mind. You will have enough in it and will need no further consolation during your terror:
> The blood of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, cleanses us from all our sins. <note>original: "Das Blut JEsu Christi des Sohns GOttes machet uns rein von allen unsern Sünden."</note> 1 John 1:7.

Wrap all your senses within this verse and let no other thoughts depart from you. Let the Devil push into you whatever he wishes through his **imagination**; <term>In Böhme’s writing, "imagination" is not just fantasy, but a creative spiritual power that can "shape" a person's inner reality for good or ill</term> just think to yourself: everything the Devil says is a lie, but this verse is true. Hold this verse as your own and let him push in whatever he wants.

58. In the event of such terror, do not go looking for many verses. He is too cunning for you; he will tear the first and best one out of your heart so that you forget it or doubt it. Just wrap your soul in this single one; it is strong enough to resist him. If you wrap your soul in it, you may well mock him. He cannot touch you, nor will he wait around for long. If you only do not give way to him, he will become a laughingstock before his fellow servants in man, and also before the Holy Angels. Indeed, he will flee from all things before you even begin to mock him.

59. Repeat the verse, take it into your heart, and draw a defiant courage against him. The Spirit that dwells within the verse will surely stand by you. Even if the soul trembles before him, stand in wrath against him as if you are risking your life; nothing will happen to you. He is not permitted to use any power, nor does he have any; as long as a person lives in this time, the Devil may do nothing to them. For Christ has opened the **Door of Grace**, <note>The "Gnaden-Thür" is a recurring image in Böhme, representing the accessible path to God’s love that remains open to any living soul regardless of their past sins</note> which stands open to the poor sinner as long as he lives on earth; that same Door of Grace is open within the human soul.

60. Christ has shattered the strong lock (which was bolted shut in God’s wrath) within his own soul. Now all souls <term>inqualiren</term> <note>A term Böhme coined from the Latin *in-qualis*; it describes how different qualities or spirits "inter-work," "co-operate," or flow into one another like branches on a single tree</note> with one another; they all come from one, and are all together only a single tree with many branches. His shattering of the lock has extended to all souls, from him back to Adam and down to the last human being. The Door of Grace stands open to everyone; God has barred it to no one, except to those who do not wish to enter. The sign of his entry into humanity is manifest to all souls; that will also be a testimony against the godless on the Day of Judgment: that they despised it.

had. Even if our sin were blood-red (as Isaiah says), the **Door of Grace** still stands open for him: For if he turns back, it shall become snow-white like wool. <note>Isaiah 1:18: "Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow."</note> Furthermore, Isaiah says in chapter 49:15-16: "Can a mother forget her child, so as not to have mercy on the son of her womb? And even if she were to forget, yet I will not forget you: For behold, I have marked you in my hands," namely in his hands pierced through by nails, and in his hollow side he has marked the soul of all souls.

61. If any soul now refuses to come and rest within this, choosing instead to despise the **mark** of Christ or let the Devil obscure it, that soul is itself at fault. Even if he should obscure it, it is nevertheless grafted into the greatest sinner in the world. For Isaiah says in the Spirit of Christ: Even if a mother were to forget her child (which would be a painful thing to happen), yet his love and grace shall not be forgotten. He has not forgotten the soul, even if it were blood-red in sins; for he has etched it into his blood and death—not just a few souls, but the whole Tree with its root and branches. As sin came from one upon all, so also righteousness comes through Christ upon all, says the Apostle. <note>A reference to Romans 5:18.</note> Just as sin pressed from one upon all leading to death, so also righteousness pressed from Christ out of one upon all leading to life.

62. That they do not all wish for this, however, is their own fault; they have **free will**. God wills that all people should be helped; and Psalm 5:5: "You are not a God who wills evil." Ezekiel 33:11: "As I live (says the Lord), I do not desire the death of the sinner, but rather that he turn back and live."

63. Therefore, no soul should think: "My measure of sin is full; God has forgotten me; I cannot be saved." No, He has etched the soul into his hands, into the nail-marks; it is a little branch on the great Tree of all souls, and <term>inqualiret</term> <note>original: "inqualiret." A term Böhme uses to describe how things share the same inner qualities, properties, or "source-springs" of being.</note> with all others equally, just as the branches do with the tree. While a person lives in this world, they stand in the Tree, as long as the soul is clothed with flesh and blood.

<summary>Böhme argues for the universality of grace, asserting that every human soul is "etched" into Christ's wounds and remains part of the "Tree of Souls" throughout their earthly life. He emphasizes that damnation is a result of the individual's free will to reject this grace, rather than a lack of divine mercy.</summary>

# On Spiritual Trial arising from the Temperament and the Stars.

## Summary.

64. Not all spiritual trials come from the Devil. 65. Even the holiest of souls can often become sad. 66. It is far more glorious to overcome during this life than afterward. 67. Terror often comes from a bad alignment of the stars, especially when the soul "imagines" <note>In Böhme’s writing, "to imagine" is not just to dream, but to sink one's spiritual focus or "will" into a specific state.</note> into its temperament. 68. 69. The *Spirit of the World* <note>original: "Spir. M." or Spiritus Mundi; the external, physical spirit of the universe.</note> then performs its illusions within it. 70. Sadness comes from the temperament, not from God's wrath. 71. An ungodly person is reckless and flippant. 72. God does not wish to reveal His wrath in this life. 73. Let the sorrowful soul simply take hold of love. 74. That the soul desires God is the "drawing of the Father," 75. and the Holy Spirit is that desire itself. 76. Therefore, we should not be faint-hearted, 77. but keep the example of the Prodigal Son before our eyes. 78. The cause of sadness. 79. The Author’s own example. 80. 81. We must fight for the Victor's Wreath. 82. God hides Himself at times 83. so that the soul shall knock and seek. 84. God's promises must be more certain. 85. What true faith is. 86. The soul must stand firm 87. and not fixate its "imagination" into its temperament. 88. Think: you stand in God's vineyard. 89. True faith. 90. Fear arises in the soul from fantasy; 91. therefore, it should not fixate upon God's wrath, 92. nor read books of religious controversy, 93. but stay with the Scriptures 94. 95. and seek the **Center of Nature** <note>original: "Centrum Naturæ"; Böhme's term for the inner source or "wheel" from which life and spirit emerge</note> with constant prayer; 96. but above all, flee from drunkenness, 97. so that God's wrath is not ignited; 98. 99. likewise, guard against anger, which is its greatest poison, as well as earnestly departing from greed. 100. 101. Within the fear of God, a **Melancholy mind** is very good; 102. therefore, it should do nothing without prayer. 103.

64. Spiritual trials do not all come from the Devil (especially in the case of **Melancholy** people). Most sadness comes from the "imagination" of the soul, when it must reside in a Melancholic lodging; there it easily becomes sad and thinks God has forgotten it, or that He does not want it. For the Melancholic temperament <note>original: "Complexion"; the traditional medical theory that human personality is governed by four bodily fluids: Sanguine, Choleric, Phlegmatic, and Melancholic.</note> is dark; it has no light of its own like the others, yet it does not belong to the essence of the soul. In this time of outward life, it is merely the soul's dwelling-house. Likewise, the soul’s holiness and righteousness do not reside in the temperament, but in heaven with God. For Saint Paul says: (Philippians 3:20) *Our conversation is in heaven.* This heaven, where God dwells—

77. 78. The sorrowful soul is troubled for this reason: that she cannot awaken great joy in her heart through her desire; she groans and laments, thinking God does not want her when she can feel nothing. In that very will-spirit, the pearl is received, so that the soul’s fire always remains in a state of desire. 88. ### IX. The Way to Christ.

<margin>Luke 11: 13.</margin>
This is what the mouth of Christ himself said: "When he comes, he will lead you into all truth; for he will take from what is mine and declare it to you." <margin>John 16: 13, 14.</margin>

90. But so that you do not doubt, be as certain of this as you are that the **temptation** <note>original: "Anfechtung"—a term for spiritual trials or "assaults" from the devil that cause doubt.</note> and the terror come only from your **complexion** <term>Complexion: The four humors or temperaments (melancholic, phlegmatic, sanguine, and choleric). Böhme believed our physical makeup shapes how we experience spiritual reality.</term>: I will set before you an example (one which is quite likely to happen to a "fiery" complexion, and even more so to a "melancholic" one). If you walk at night in a dark room, you become terrified and constantly think there is something in the darkness that might scare you. What kind of fear is this? Does the flesh fear? No, otherwise it would not go in; rather, the poor soul, imprisoned in the flesh, is afraid in the darkness. It is constantly worried that the devil might grab it, for it knows that he dwells in the darkness—and so the fear is that he will reach for it. Here it is easy to see that the fear comes from the **fantasy** <note>The "fantasy" or "imagination" is the mind's power to create internal images. Böhme warns that the soul can "eat" these images, leading to peace or to terror.</note>. This is exactly how it goes for the poor soul in a perpetual, dark "complexion-chamber"; it is so timid because it must dwell in the darkness, and it constantly fears the devil and **God's** wrath.

91. A soul in the "melancholic chamber" should by no means speculate on **God's** wrath, nor should such a person like to be alone, but rather should stay among people who are talking. In this way, the soul takes the "fantasy" of the conversation into itself and does not speculate—for no speculation is useful to it. If the soul cannot apply such speculation to its own salvation, it should let it be.

92. Such a person should also not read any writings that teach about a **particular election** <note>original: "sonderlichen Wahl"—referring to the doctrine of predestination. Böhme is warning that reading about whether God has "pre-chosen" certain people for salvation or damnation can drive a melancholic person to despair.</note>. These authors all teach without understanding and do not explain it correctly, as the high tongue of the **Holy Spirit** understands and has established it, and as has been sufficiently demonstrated in our other writings.

93. One should not make use of many different kinds of writings, but simply stay with the Scripture, where a firm comfort may be found.
